pages.html:/repos/AleFunky/gd3ds/readme:
Geometry Dash for the 3DS

This is a demake of the popular mobile game Geometry Dash for the Nintendo 3DS.

Geometry Dash and its respective resources are by RobTop Games.

Features

  • [x] Main levels up to Theory of Everything 2
  • [x] Gameplay
  • [x] Accurate physics
  • [x] Hitbox display
  • [x] Click-On-Steps functionality
  • [x] Particles
  • [x] Player trails
  • [x] Practice mode
  • [x] Practice music sync
  • [x] Level coins
  • [x] Settings and Icon Saving
  • [x] Progress tracking and Statistics
  • [x] 3D support
  • [x] Dual-screen UI
  • [x] 1.9 Custom Level Importing (via SD Card)
  • [x] Bottom screen tap effects
  • [x] Icons on the Title Screen
  • [x] Various in-game visual effects and UI animations
  • [x] Auto-Checkpoints
  • [x] Better bottom screen HUD
  • [ ] Online support
  • [ ] Start position support

Features that aren't planned but may be added either way

  • [ ] Achievements
  • [ ] Touchscreen-less navigation options
  • [ ] Dual death effect
  • [ ] Size portal lightning effect
  • [ ] Portal flash effect upon use
  • [ ] Gravity switch effect
  • [ ] Startpos switcher
  • [ ] Cheat display

Additional Credits

  • camila314 - Pathfinder Mod's physics

Download

The current release is available on Universal Updater. Alternatively, you can manually download both the .3dsx and the .cia files here, or you can scan the QR code below in FBI to install the game to your home menu automatically.

Discord

You can visit our Discord server and get support (or talk if you want to): Discord

Licensing

All original assets and source code of this project are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-Sharealike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0) - meaning you can redistribute and transform them as long as give appropriate credit, indicate any changes made and distribute your contributions under the same license.
Code and assets adapted from other open-source projects belong to their respective authors and are licensed under the same terms as the source material.
All original Geometry Dash game assets belong to RobTob Games AB and RobTop Games AB only.

FAQ

How do I install this on my 3DS?

The current easiest way is to open the Universal Updater app on your 3DS and download the game from there. If you prefer doing it manually, download either the .3dsx or .cia file from the releases page and place it on your SD Card, then depending on which file you chose, launch it through the Homebrew Launcher, or install it to your home menu through FBI.

The game is saying something about "missing DSP firmware", what do I do?

If you're playing on actual hardware this shouldn't be an issue as most 3DS homebrew tutorials dump this file in the process. If you're playing on an emulator, navigate to (your emulator's data folder)\sdmc\3ds\ and create a file named dspfirm.cdc in said location. It can be completely empty for all the emulator cares, it just has to be present. In case you're running into this error on a real console, open the Luma menu (usually accessed by pressing L, DPAD DOWN and SELECT at the same time), scroll to Miscellaneous options... and press Dump DSP firmware.

How do I play / add custom levels?

You'll need to either export a copy of your level of choice using the GDShare Geode mod or download an archive of said level from GDHistory. If the level uses a custom song, you'll also need to either extract it from your Geometry Dash songs folder (%localappdata%\GeometryDash on Windows), or download it separately from Newgrounds. Once you have the level .gmd (and song, renamed to its Newgrounds ID) prepared, copy them to \3ds\gd3ds\external_levels\ and \3ds\gd3ds\saved_songs\ on your SD Card respectively. Putting the level files into additional folders within the main \external_levels\ directory is supported. Do keep in mind, however, that any objects from updates 2.0 and above will not load, and object-heavy levels are not guaranteed to be playable - especially on non-New 3DS models.

Are you going to add a level editor?

The short answer is no. The long answer is that it's simply too much work for something that would run poorly on the already underpowered 3DS hardware, would be unable to upload levels to the Geometry Dash servers and that 99% of people would not care about.

Can you add X feature / X gamemode / X level?

Everything that's planned to be implemented is listed in the planned features section above - in short, anything major from updates above 1.9 will not be added. However, if you come up with an improvement or a quality of life feature the game could use, you're welcome to suggest it in the Discord server.

Why not add 2.0 / 2.1 / 2.2 / whatever?

Theoretically all features up to 2.1 ARE possible to implement, but they'd be a large undertaking to add in an adequately performant and accurate way. 2.2 only amplifies these concerns, not to mention it having some features that are fully impossible to have work faithfully on 3DS hardware (namely, shader triggers). Many 1.9 levels already struggle to run on the original 3DS, due to their high object counts, and future updates, with moving objects and much more decoration, exponentially worsen this issue.

pages.html:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/:
Checkpoint

A fast and simple homebrew save management framework for 3DS and Switch, written in C++.

Why use Checkpoint?

Checkpoint is created following ideas of simplicity and efficiency. The UI has been designed to condense as many options as possible, while keeping it simple to work with.

Moreover, Checkpoint is extremely lightweight - while being packaged with a nice graphic user interface - and is built using the most recent libraries available.

Checkpoint doesn't rely on external title lists or filters to work: titles are detected and filtered automatically, so it doesn't need constant user maintenance to retain full functionality.

Checkpoint is a framework, not just an app: everything it can do to a save is also reachable from scripts you can write yourself and drop on the SD card, so the console can do things no release ever shipped with. See Scripting.

Features

Checkpoint backs up and restores save data for:

  • 3DS: 3DS cartridges and digital titles (including demos), extdata, DS cartridges, DSiWare and GBA Virtual Console titles
  • Switch: saves for the titles you have played, with title information loaded automatically

Both versions share the same core feature set:

  • A completely redesigned user interface, with light and dark mode theming
  • A Settings section to configure everything directly from the console: favorites, filters, additional save folders and more, with no manual file editing required
  • Internationalization support: English, Italian, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, Japanese and Chinese
  • Fast, responsive file operations: backups and restores run on a worker thread, and backups can be cancelled while in progress
  • Additional save folders, configurable per title through a built-in folder browser
  • A background FTP server, to access your save backups directly from your PC
  • Wireless save transfer between consoles
  • A scripting engine, with bundled scripts for cheat management and Google Drive save sync, and a documented API for writing your own
  • An HTTP log server, to view Checkpoint's logs in real time from any browser on your network

On Switch, Checkpoint also provides:

  • A rendering backend built on deko3d, which makes the application ~70% smaller than before
  • 1080p docked mode support, alongside 720p in handheld
  • A USB MTP server, which makes the console show up as a portable device on your PC so you can drag backups off over the charging cable, with no network involved
  • File-by-file verification after restore, and safer handling of large save restores

Scripting

Checkpoint runs scripts written in C, interpreted on the console. A script is a single .c file on the SD card: no compiler, no rebuild, no reflash. Put it in the right folder and it shows up in the Scripts menu (SELECT on 3DS, Minus on Switch) the next time you launch the app.

Scripts get a native API — #include <checkpoint.h> — that reaches the same machinery the app itself uses:

  • Titles: the whole catalog, ids, names, product codes, cart/save/extdata flags, backup folders
  • Save data: open a title's save (or 3DS extdata, or console-wide shared extdata), then read, write, delete, list and commit files inside it, and create, rename or remove its folders
  • SD card: directory listings, mkdir -p, existence checks, plus ordinary C file I/O
  • Zip: pack or unpack a folder with the same store-only framing the wireless transfer and chlink use
  • Network: HTTP GET, full requests with methods, headers and bodies, and streamed file uploads
  • JSON: parse and walk documents
  • UI: messages, confirmations, single and multiple choice pickers, keyboard and numeric keypad, a status line and nested progress bars, all rendered by Checkpoint itself
  • Plus picoc's C standard library: stdio, stdlib, string, unistd, ctype, math, time

A running script owns the screen: its output streams into a scrollable log pane while its dialogs and progress bars take the other screen (3DS) or a card over the transcript (Switch). Holding B aborts any script, even one stuck in an infinite loop, without rebooting the console.

A few scripts ship with the app already:

  • browser — file browser for the SD card and for a title's live save archive: copy, move, rename, delete, make folders, read properties, zip and unzip, one item or a batch at a time, with either side of a transfer on the card or inside a save
  • sharkive — cheat manager: downloads the Sharkive database, lets you tick cheats per title, and writes the cheat files Luma3DS (3DS) or Atmosphere (Switch) expect
  • googledrive — backs up your save backups to your own Google Drive, with a device-code sign-in and per-backup zips (setup guide)
  • webdav — the same for any WebDAV server you already have (Nextcloud, Synology, rclone serve webdav, …): uploads only what isn't there yet, and can download a backup back onto the console (setup guide)
  • playcoins — sets the console's Play Coins (3DS)
  • extdata — creates the extdata archive a title has never written, so an extdata backup has somewhere to restore into (3DS)
  • notifications — backs up and restores everything behind the Notifications applet, the SpotPass content and the notification list alike, none of which belongs to a title (3DS)

Writing your own is documented in full in scripts/README.md: the API reference, the interpreter's limits, recipes, and a checklist for both human and AI authors. scripts/examples/example.c is a runnable guided tour, one menu entry per API area. Before copying a script to the SD card, parse-check it on your PC with tools/scriptlint.sh.

chlink

Checkpoint comes with chlink, a companion command line app for your PC that talks to Checkpoint's wireless save transfer feature. With chlink you can send save backups from your PC to the console and receive backups from the console to your PC, over your local network - no cables and no SD card swapping required.

Transfers are protected by a 4-digit PIN displayed on the console, and chlink automatically recognizes backups coming from a Checkpoint SD card layout, so title and backup information are filled in for you.

chlink is a single, dependency-free executable available for Windows, macOS and Linux. You can download it from the releases page, or build it yourself from the tools/chlink folder.

Usage

You can use Checkpoint for 3DS with both cfw and Rosalina-based Homebrew Launchers. *hax-based Homebrew Launchers are not supported by Checkpoint.

Checkpoint for Switch runs on homebrew launcher. Make sure you're running up-to-date payloads.

The first launch will take longer than usual, due to the working directories being created - Checkpoint will be significantly faster upon launch from then on.

Working path

Checkpoint relies on the following folders to store the files it generates. Note that all the working directories are automatically generated on first launch (or when Checkpoint finds a new title that doesn't have a working directory yet).

3DS

  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint: root path
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/config.json: configuration file
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/logs: log files
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/saves/<unique id> <game title>: root path for all the save backups for a generic game
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/extdata/<unique id> <game title>: root path for all the extdata backups for a generic game
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/scripts/universal: your own scripts, offered for every title
  • sdmc:/3ds/Checkpoint/scripts/<title id>: your own scripts, offered for that title only

Switch

  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint: root path
  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint/config.json: configuration file
  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint/logs: log files
  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint/saves/<title id> <game title>: root path for all the save backups for a generic game
  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint/scripts/universal: your own scripts, offered for every title
  • sdmc:/switch/Checkpoint/scripts/<title id>: your own scripts, offered for that title only

Configuration

All the options that used to require manual edits to the configuration file can now be managed from the Settings section, directly on the console. The config.json file is still stored in Checkpoint's working directory, but you're not required to touch it anymore.

Troubleshooting

Checkpoint displays error codes when something weird happens or operations fail. If you have any issues, please ensure they haven't already been addressed, and report the error code and a summary of your operations to reproduce it.

Additionally, you can receive real-time support by joining FlagBrew's Discord server (link below).

Building

devkitARM and devkitA64 are required to compile Checkpoint for 3DS and Switch, respectively. Learn more at devkitpro.org. Install or update dependencies as follows.

The scripting engine lives in a submodule, so a fresh clone needs:

git submodule update --init --recursive

3DS version

dkp-pacman -S libctru citro3d citro2d tex3ds 3ds-curl 3ds-mbedtls

Switch version

dkp-pacman -S libnx switch-pkg-config deko3d switch-harfbuzz switch-freetype switch-libjpeg-turbo switch-curl switch-mbedtls

Build from the repository root with make 3ds or make switch.

License

This project is licensed under the GNU GPLv3. Additional Terms 7.b and 7.c of GPLv3 apply to this. See LICENSE.md for details.

Credits

  • Bernardo for creating Checkpoint.
  • J-D-K for the original JKSM version.
  • TuxSH for TWLSaveTool, from which SPI code has been taken.
  • LiquidFenrir for the GBA Virtual Console save support.
  • SNBeast for the DSiWare save support proof of concept.
  • mtheall for ftpd's code used as reference for our FTP implementation.
  • edu1010 for the wireless save transfer feature.
  • piepie62 and all other PKSM contributors for some code that has been ported to Checkpoint.
  • zsaleeba for being the original contributor to picoc, the C interpreter Checkpoint's scripting engine is built on, and all the contributors to FlagBrew's flavor of picoc, which is the fork this project relies on.
  • WinterMute, fincs and devkitPro contributors for devkitARM, devkitA64 and dkp-pacman.
  • Yellows8 and all the mantainers for switch-examples.
  • rakujira for the awesome Checkpoint logo.
  • achinech for helping to debug the infamous 3.8.x crash issue.
  • Fellow testers and troubleshooters for their help.
  • The huge amount of supporters that this project has gained over the years.

Without you, this project wouldn't have existed. Thank you.

json:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/.body: ### 3DS: What's new - Added: **WarioWare: D.I.Y. save backup and restore**. Its 16 MB save lives in NAND inside the cartridge instead of on a save chip, where no 3DS save interface can reach it. Checkpoint now talks to the cartridge directly, so you back it up and restore it from the title list like any other DS cart: no GodMode9i, no rebooting into DS mode. - This is particularly exciting because the strategy used to allow this functionality without rebooting in DS mode is brand new and this was thought to be impossible to achieve in the past. - A backup takes about a minute. A restore only rewrites the pages that differ from what is already on the cartridge, and reads every page it writes back to verify it. Restoring the backup you just made writes nothing at all; the worst case, where every page differs, takes about 6.5 minutes. - Checkpoint's dumps were checked byte for byte against GodMode9i's dumps of the same cartridge. - **The CIA build is required.** The 3DSX build can't reach the cartridge controller, so it refuses instead of reading. - So far this has been tested on one European cartridge. Other regions, and the other carts that save the same way, are recognised but not verified yet: *please* report back. - Don't remove the cartridge or turn off the console during a restore. Pages that were already written stay written, so an interrupted restore leaves the save half old and half new until you run it again. - Fixed: DS cart backups no longer fail at random while writing to the SD card. - Fixed: backing up the extdata of the theme entries no longer fails. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### Switch: What's new - Fixed: **restoring a save no longer inflates it to over 64 MB**. Since 5.1.0, every restore extended the save data area by its safety margin even when the backup already fit, so a 2 MB save came back at 65 MB. The area is now extended only when the backup actually needs more room than it has. - Fixed: **Checkpoint now opens on the profile it was launched under**, instead of always starting on the first user. A title override uses the profile you picked at launch; applet mode uses the profile that last opened a game. - Fixed: **the account picker can now be reached with the controller**. The avatar at the bottom of the sidebar is part of the sidebar cursor now: press Down past the settings gear. ZL still opens it too. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### Wireless transfer: What's new - Added: **a configurable server port**, in Settings > Network (3DS) / Connectivity (Switch), under **Server port**. - 8000 is still the default. Change it when another program already holds that port. - The port is shared by the wireless receiver and the log server, and takes effect the next time Checkpoint starts. Anything from 1024 to 65535 is accepted. - The Receive screen shows the port, as before. chlink takes it with `--port`, or as `--to :`. ### Scripting: What's new - Fixed: **webdav now works with Synology's WebDAV Server**. Synology accepted the login and then answered the folder check with a 403, because the request named the folder without its trailing `/`. Folders are now always requested with the slash, which is the form the WebDAV spec tells clients to use. --- If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated. --- --- [![Discord](https://discordapp.com/api/guilds/278222834633801728/widget.png?style=banner3&time-)](https://discord.gg/bGKEyfY)

3DS: What's new

  • Added: WarioWare: D.I.Y. save backup and restore. Its 16 MB save lives in NAND inside the cartridge instead of on a save chip, where no 3DS save interface can reach it. Checkpoint now talks to the cartridge directly, so you back it up and restore it from the title list like any other DS cart: no GodMode9i, no rebooting into DS mode.
    • This is particularly exciting because the strategy used to allow this functionality without rebooting in DS mode is brand new and this was thought to be impossible to achieve in the past.
    • A backup takes about a minute. A restore only rewrites the pages that differ from what is already on the cartridge, and reads every page it writes back to verify it. Restoring the backup you just made writes nothing at all; the worst case, where every page differs, takes about 6.5 minutes.
    • Checkpoint's dumps were checked byte for byte against GodMode9i's dumps of the same cartridge.
    • The CIA build is required. The 3DSX build can't reach the cartridge controller, so it refuses instead of reading.
    • So far this has been tested on one European cartridge. Other regions, and the other carts that save the same way, are recognised but not verified yet: please report back.
    • Don't remove the cartridge or turn off the console during a restore. Pages that were already written stay written, so an interrupted restore leaves the save half old and half new until you run it again.
  • Fixed: DS cart backups no longer fail at random while writing to the SD card.
  • Fixed: backing up the extdata of the theme entries no longer fails.
  • General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

Switch: What's new

  • Fixed: restoring a save no longer inflates it to over 64 MB. Since 5.1.0, every restore extended the save data area by its safety margin even when the backup already fit, so a 2 MB save came back at 65 MB. The area is now extended only when the backup actually needs more room than it has.
  • Fixed: Checkpoint now opens on the profile it was launched under, instead of always starting on the first user. A title override uses the profile you picked at launch; applet mode uses the profile that last opened a game.
  • Fixed: the account picker can now be reached with the controller. The avatar at the bottom of the sidebar is part of the sidebar cursor now: press Down past the settings gear. ZL still opens it too.
  • General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

Wireless transfer: What's new

  • Added: a configurable server port, in Settings > Network (3DS) / Connectivity (Switch), under Server port.
    • 8000 is still the default. Change it when another program already holds that port.
    • The port is shared by the wireless receiver and the log server, and takes effect the next time Checkpoint starts. Anything from 1024 to 65535 is accepted.
    • The Receive screen shows the port, as before. chlink takes it with --port, or as --to <ip>:<port>.

Scripting: What's new

  • Fixed: webdav now works with Synology's WebDAV Server. Synology accepted the login and then answered the folder check with a 403, because the request named the folder without its trailing /. Folders are now always requested with the slash, which is the form the WebDAV spec tells clients to use.

If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated.

json:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/.name: Checkpoint 5.2.0
json:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/.body: ### Updates: What's new - Added: **autoupdater** (#106). - The check runs in the background, so the title list still loads while it happens. Nothing is ever installed without you agreeing to it first. - Automatic updates are on by default and can be turned off in Settings. - Fun fact: this was the oldest open feature request on the repository. It was filed in June 2018. Eight years is a long time to wait, but here it is. ### Switch: What's new - Added: **MTP USB transfers**. Plug the console into your PC with the charging cable and Checkpoint shows up as a portable device, exactly like a phone or a camera does. - Turn it on in Settings > Connectivity, under **USB (MTP)**. It's off by default, and the line underneath tells you its status: waiting for a PC, connected, or USB unavailable. - USB unavailable usually means the console is docked or something else has already claimed the port. Checkpoint keeps trying in the background, so undocking is enough: no restart needed. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### 3DS: What's new - Added: **the Internet Browser is back in the title list** (#579), so its save data can be backed up and restored like any other title's. The old core is gone, replaced with the latest source code from [mtheall](https://github.com/mtheall)'s [ftpd](https://github.com/mtheall/ftpd), which has been adapted to properly fit in Checkpoint. - Fixed: **3DS transfers are roughly 4x faster on upload and 2x on download**. The bottleneck was synchronous socket calls stalling the transfer thread, so the console now overlaps disk and network work instead of alternating between them. - You'll notice the UI being a bit less responsive on the 3DS when FTP transfers are running: this is completely normal. - Fixed: the Switch server no longer exhausts the system's socket buffers during a folder upload, which left it unable to accept new data connections until it timed out. - Fixed: turning FTP off in Settings now closes the listening socket and drops the sessions, instead of leaving the port open. ### Scripting: What's new - Added: **browser**, a file browser for the SD card *and* for a title's live save archive. - It supports copy, move, rename, delete, make folders, read properties, zip and unzip, one item or a batch at a time. - It is the practical way to reach into a save without a PC: pull one file out of an archive onto the card, drop an edited one back in, or move a folder between two titles. - Added: **extdata** (3DS), to create the extdata archive a title never made (#576). - This script solves an issue where game mods use extdata for a title that never creates them. The script allows to artificially create a new extdata archive for that title. - It also inspects any extdata id, including one a mod wrote under an id Checkpoint does not derive from the title id, and deletes an archive when you mean to. - Added: new API calls, all documented in [`scripts/README.md`](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Checkpoint/blob/master/scripts/README.md). - `sav_mkdir`, `sav_rmdir` and `sav_rename`: scripts can now shape the folder structure inside a save archive, not just read and write files in it. - `sav_open_extdata`, to open a per-title extdata archive by its raw id. - `extdata_default_id`, `extdata_create` and `extdata_delete` (3DS; they return `-1` on Switch). `extdata_create` refuses to touch an archive that already exists, so a mistyped id cannot erase a save. - Fixed: the 3DS title catalog handed to scripts now also holds the titles that appear in the Extdata list alone. - Fixed: `strdup` allocates on the same run-scoped heap as `malloc`, so `free()` releases it and an aborted run reclaims it. ### Wireless transfer: What's new - Added: **a fixed Receive PIN**, in Settings > Network (3DS) / Connectivity (Switch). - The PIN is still random per receive by default. Pin one and a `chlink send --pin 1234` baked into a script keeps working run after run, which is what makes unattended batch transfers from the PC possible. - Fixed: **`chlink send` failing with "receiver rejected the PIN (403): Invalid token"** (#561). Go canonicalises header names before writing them, so the console's case-sensitive lookup never found the token header and rejected every upload. - Fixed: a backup received from a sender that identifies no installed title no longer lands in an "Unknown title" folder (#572). It goes to the title whose backup list you opened Receive from, which is the one you pointed at. - Fixed: the receiver no longer logs a connection in progress as an error, and no longer floods the log during a transfer. ### 3DS: What's new - Fixed: **a restore that cannot fit the console's path limit is refused before anything is deleted**. It used to wipe the save archive first and die afterwards, on a backup folder the filesystem was never going to accept. Both the copy roots and every entry under them are checked up front, and the message names the offending path. - Fixed: **files a desktop OS left next to your backup no longer break a restore** (#577). macOS stores a file's extended attributes in a `._` sidecar next to it on FAT/exFAT, and drops `.DS_Store` in every folder Finder opens; a restore hit one *after* it had already cleared the console-side save. Those, and the equivalents Windows leaves behind, are now filtered out of the copy. - Fixed: **carts whose save lives in on-cart NAND are now identified** (#553, WarioWare: D.I.Y. and friends). They have no SPI save chip, so the probe used to report a bogus capacity and back up whatever the bus returned. Checkpoint now says what the cart is and points at GodMode9i in DS mode, rather than failing with a save archive error. - Fixed: **the progress modal no longer looks frozen while a restore clears the destination** (#559). Clearing an extdata archive of thousands of files is now its own progress stage, and the stage labels (Backup, Restore, Clearing, Sending...) are translated. - Fixed: buttons no longer do anything while the title list is still loading (#565). You could back up or restore a title you could not see yet, against a selection that was about to move. - Added: **Simplified Chinese is selectable in Settings** (#566, thanks @dragonflylee). The translation shipped in 5.0.0 but the 3DS language list never offered it. - Added: New 3DS consoles also run their application cores at 804 MHz now. This is a no-op on Old 3DS and 2DS. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### Switch: What's new - Fixed: **restoring a save of tens of thousands of small files no longer stalls near the end**. - The save data area is extended when the backup needs more room than it has. - Files are preallocated instead of being grown block by block, and the free space is checked against the cluster-rounded requirement after the wipe, so the restore refuses up front instead of dying at 95%. - The copy is counted against the pre-flight scan: a restore that reports success but moved fewer files than the backup holds is now reported as the failure it is. - Save partition space is logged at every step, so a restore that still fails can be diagnosed from the log. - Fixed: **restore verification is about twice as fast**. The CRC of each file is taken from the bytes already in the copy buffer, so the verify pass re-reads only the committed save instead of both sides. - Fixed: **the console no longer goes to sleep in the middle of a backup, restore or transfer** (#574). Sleeping suspended the process mid-copy, on the save filesystem, with a journal half committed. Only auto-sleep is held off: the screen still dims on its usual idle delay. - Added: the selection ring and the grid now animate between tiles instead of jumping, and snap when what is underneath changes (a different save type filter, a different account). - Fixed: the same progress and stage-label work as the 3DS side (#559). - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### Translations - Added: **Russian** translation (thanks @Waleri228) - Current language support includes English, Italian, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Russian. - If you're a native speaker and think that text wording and appearance in the UI can be improved, please submit a pull request or open an issue on this repository. --- If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated. --- --- [![Discord](https://discordapp.com/api/guilds/278222834633801728/widget.png?style=banner3&time-)](https://discord.gg/bGKEyfY)

json:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/.body: Checkpoint 4.0.0 was the largest update the app ever had. Version 5.0.0 redefines what the app ***is***. Checkpoint is now a save management **framework**: everything it can do to a save is also reachable from scripts you write yourself and drop on the SD card, so your console can do things no release of Checkpoint ever shipped with. The cheat manager is back as one of those scripts, and so is cloud save sync, to Google Drive, or to any WebDAV server you already run. Enjoy! ### Scripting: What's new - Added: **a scripting engine**. Checkpoint runs C scripts, interpreted on the console. A script is a single `.c` file on the SD card: no compiler, no rebuild, no reflash. - Scripts live in `sdmc:/<3ds|switch>/Checkpoint/scripts/universal` to be offered for every title, or in `scripts/` to be offered for that title only. - Added: a new **Scripts menu**, reachable with **SELECT** on 3DS and **Minus** on Switch. - Scripts get a native API through `#include <checkpoint.h>`, reaching the same functions the app itself uses: the title catalog, save archives (3DS extdata and shared extdata included) to read, write, delete, list and commit files into, SD card I/O, zip pack and unpack, HTTP requests and streamed file uploads, JSON parsing, and UI dialogs rendered by Checkpoint itself. - Added: **a console UI for scripts**. A running script owns the screen: its output streams into a scrollable log pane, while its messages, confirmations, pickers, keyboards and nested progress bars take the other screen on 3DS, or a card over the transcript on Switch. - Added: **script cancellation**. Holding **B** aborts any script, even one stuck in an infinite loop, without rebooting the console. - Added: **a sealing API**, to let scripts store secrets like tokens and passwords on the SD card encrypted with a console-bound key, and optionally with a passphrase of your choice. - Scripts also get picoc's C standard library: `stdio`, `stdlib`, `string`, `unistd`, `ctype`, `math` and `time`. - Added: **full scripting documentation**, in [`scripts/README.md`](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Checkpoint/blob/master/scripts/README.md): the API reference, the interpreter's limits, recipes, and a checklist for both human and AI script authors. - [`scripts/examples/example.c`](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Checkpoint/blob/master/scripts/examples/example.c) is a runnable guided tour of the API, one menu entry per area. - `tools/scriptlint.sh` parse-checks your scripts on your PC, before you copy them onto the SD card. - Fixed: exceptions thrown while a script runs are caught and reported to you, instead of terminating the app non-deterministically. ### Bundled scripts - Added: **sharkive**, and with it the **cheat manager is back**. - It downloads the latest [Sharkive](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Sharkive) database, lets you pick cheats per title, and writes the cheat files Luma3DS (3DS) and Atmosphere (Switch) expect. - Because it is a script now, the cheat database follows Sharkive instead of waiting for a Checkpoint release. This solves one of the maintenance problems that made the feature go away in 4.0.0. - Note: if you're not satisfied with the cheats distributed in Sharkive, you can submit issues and patches to the repo itself, or contribute by writing a script that downloads cheats from another provider. Checkpoint is really open to contributions. - Added: **googledrive**, to sync your save backups to your own Google Drive. - Sign-in happens through Google's device flow: the console shows a code, you type it on your phone or PC. - Sync everything, a single title, or a single backup. Each backup is uploaded as a zip, and already uploaded backups are skipped. - Your credentials are sealed with the new encryption API, so they never sit on the SD card in the clear. Setup instructions are in [`scripts/googledrive.md`](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Checkpoint/blob/master/scripts/googledrive.md). - Added: **webdav**, to sync those same backups to any WebDAV server you already run: Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology, Apache `mod_dav`, `rclone serve webdav`, most NAS "personal cloud" apps. - Upload every title, one title, or a single backup, skipping what is already on the server. It can also pull a backup back down onto the console, where Checkpoint's usual Restore takes over. - Credentials are sealed with the encryption API, like Drive's. Setup, with the right base URL for each common server, is in [`scripts/webdav.md`](https://github.com/FlagBrew/Checkpoint/blob/master/scripts/webdav.md); `tools/webdav-testserver.py` gives you a throwaway server on your PC to try the whole round trip against first. - Added: **playcoins**, to set the console's Play Coins (3DS). - Note: the play coins management feature is now available via scripts only. ### 3DS: What's new - Added: a menu overlay to reach Settings and Scripts. - Fixed: **GBA Virtual Console saves now move between consoles** (#557). A backup used to be the whole console-side container, signed for the console that made it, so restoring it anywhere else failed, or reported success and left the game's own save untouched. - A backup is now the bare save file, the same 512 B to 128 KB `.sav` an emulator or GodMode9 reads, and restoring writes it back into the container and re-signs it for the console doing the restoring. - Backups taken by older versions of Checkpoint still restore. - Fixed: Checkpoint now runs on emulators. The Rosalina `hb:ldr` check is skipped when an emulator is detected, instead of refusing to boot. - Fixed: modal dialogs now measure and lay out their text properly, so larger text and translated strings are not clipped anymore. - Fixed: a memory corruption in the choice overlay's callback. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### Switch: What's new - Added: a Scripts entry in the sidebar, and a menu overlay to reach Settings and Scripts. - Fixed: the app doesn't hang anymore when the account selector is opened while backup sizes are still being computed. The size worker now pauses while the applet is up. - Fixed: truncated backup names in the backup list. - Fixed: modal dialogs now measure and lay out their text properly, so larger text and translated strings are not clipped anymore. - Fixed: threads are torn down properly when the app is forced to exit. - Fixed: unhandled exceptions are logged with far more detail, so crashes can actually be diagnosed from the log. - General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience. ### chlink: What's new - Fixed: a backup that travels as a single file instead of a zip -- a DS cart save, a GBA VC save -- arrived with the dot stripped out of its name (`00000001 sav`), and nothing could restore it afterwards. The receiving side keeps the extension now, on both consoles and in chlink. - Backups already received with a mangled name are not lost: a raw backup folder holding a single file is restored whatever that file is called. - Added: the receiver logs each stored file with its size and destination, and says how far it got when a transfer fails. ### Translations - Added: **Simplified Chinese** translation (thanks @JeanPhoenixWong) - Current language support includes English, Italian, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, Japanese and Simplified Chinese. - If you're a native speaker and think that text wording and appearance in the UI can be improved, please submit a pull request or open an issue on this repository. --- <img width="194" height="190" alt="qr" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b41a4bcd-a995-4f50-8a15-e8d0b73fdcb4" /> --- If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated. --- [![Discord](https://discordapp.com/api/guilds/278222834633801728/widget.png?style=banner3&time-)](https://discord.gg/bGKEyfY)

This release focuses on adding performance improvements to the 3DS version of the software.

## What's new

- **Fixed: startup time has been drastically improved: ~50% speedup on uncached boot, ~90% speedup on cached boot.**
  - This has been achieved by profiling the application boot process, and realizing that title cache persistence on the SD card took majority of the loading time. Now this operation is lazily done in a separate thread. It's funny to realize that a badly implemented optimization can become a bottleneck of its own, so take my mistake as a lesson.
  - Here's the improvements I had on my console (improvements may vary since they depend on how many games you have on your console):
    - Uncached startup went down from 9.8s to 5.7s
    - Cached startup went down from 5.7s to 0.6s
- **Added: due to requests from multiple users, Checkpoint can now be updated from Universal Updater.**
- Fixed: cartridge loading now runs immediately rather than waiting for the title cache to be persisted on the SD card.
- Fixed: properly quit the application gracefully when an handled exception occurs.
- Fixed: initial code refactoring.
- Removed: some redundant logs in the title loader.
- General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.
  
Thank you for your patience and support.

If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated.

json:/repos/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint/.body:
This release mostly  contains changes and patches related to the infamous 3.8.x startup crash issue affecting the 3DS version of the software. General improvements have been added to the Switch version as well.

## What's new

- **Fixed: the startup crash issue affecting all version since 3.8.0 has been identified and patched.**
  - Huge shoutout to achinech on Discord who volunteered to debug the issue on their console.
  - If you still encounter startup crash issues, please notify the team immediately on [Discord](https://discord.gg/bGKEyfY) and on GitHub issues.
- **Fixed: cartridge scanning has been refactored to be way more efficient.**
  - Previously, the software used to poll the cartridge synchronously for every frame of the UI thread. Cartridge scanning is now happening on a separate thread which only runs twice per second.
- Added: a more advanced threading framework ported from PKSM.
- Added: networking support and an integrated HTTP server. This is currently used to provide real-time online access to the application logs, but this code will be useful for future features like self-updating.
- Added: more robust logging ported from PKSM. Logs are stored in the `/3ds/Checkpoint/logs` folder and are split by date.
  - Logs are also accessible at runtime through the integrated HTTP server at the following addresses:
    - `http://3ds-ip-address:8000/logs/memory` for the logs of Checkpoint's current run
    - `http://3ds-ip-address:8000/logs/file` for all the logs for the current date
- Added: compiler optimizations are back. This includes link-time optimization and an upgrade from `O2` to `O3` compared to v.3.7.4.
- Fixed: better configuration file handling ported from PKSM.
- Fixed: better thread synchronization between UI thread and title loading thread.
- Fixed: wrap the entire program into try-catch blocks to prevent crashes caused by other unhandled exceptions in the future.
- Fixed: few graphics improvements.
- Fixed: readme has been updated with latest screenshots.
- General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

The source code has started to become a little bit messy, but this patch needed to be released as soon as possible. Future improvements to the software will surely focus on code and program cleanup and performance improvements. 
  
Thank you for your patience and support.

If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated.

Thank you for your patience and support.

If you wish to contribute, pull requests are highly appreciated.

commit.message:
feat: 30 fps on both screens on Old 3DS with C420 frames, even pacing, sharper MP4 (0.12.4)

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: smoother two-screen recording, bottom-screen mode, crash fixes (0.11.4 beta)

Old 3DS recordings were limited by the SD card in 3D games, and the
bottom screen paused whenever the card fell behind. Changes:

- throttling: when the SD is behind, the bottom screen drops to 2/3 of
  its rate first and the top keeps full rate; the top halves and the
  bottom pauses only with the ring nearly full (Mario Kart 7: ~22 + 11
  fps steady instead of drops and pauses);
- write blocks 512 KB (+7% SD speed), FS session at low priority, ring
  overhang instead of pad records, keyframes every ~2 s (player seeks
  adjusted), main loop sleeps until the next capture is due (audio poll
  gaps 205 ms -> 6-7 ms);
- BGR8 / RGBA8 framebuffers converted a column at a time into the cache
  while encoding (no pass over the frame through main memory);
- extended-memory games (plugin memory): the ring is mirrored right
  after its end, no pad records (~9% of the bytes);
- New 3DS: 804 MHz + L2 while recording, Q565 intra frames for frames
  that change all over, a 16-24 MB ring; top screen 800 px mode recorded
  whole (pairs of columns averaged);
- Settings -> Screens: Bottom (recording only the bottom screen);
- recording format 5: R3DQ (Q565, a QOI-style intra codec for RGB565,
  also in ARM assembly) and R3DH (Huffman over XR32) frames, read by the
  player, gallery, MP4 conversion, r3dconv and the phone page (byte for
  byte the same as C, tests/web/compare.mjs); Huffman and Q565 stay off
  on Old 3DS (no CPU time for them there);
- fix: kernel panic in svcStartInterProcessDma when a recording started
  in HOME and a game was launched: too many DMAs were open at once while
  the converter was starved. At most 4 DMAs run at once, the main thread
  closes finished ones right away, and stopping a recording stops DMAs
  still running before their buffers are freed;
- app: SD estimate ~320 MB/min (3D games), player logs sound gaps.

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: soft edges around silence in recorded audio

Before a silence the previous sound now fades out over up to one
frame (played backwards from its end, so there is no step), and the
sound after it fades in over ~2.4 ms, instead of stopping and starting
on a sample. The same in the player, the MP4 conversion, the phone
page and r3dconv; the timeline does not change. Host test added; the
phone page and r3dconv still give the same audio byte for byte.

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: encode on the game's core on Old 3DS (0.9.14 beta)

On an Old 3DS the system core has little time to spare while a game
runs, and frames were dropped waiting for the encoder. The converter
now runs on the game's core at the lowest priority, so it only takes
the time the game's threads leave idle (idea from Luma3DS-Flashback's
design notes, no code from it). Capture, the SD writer and audio stay
on the system core; New 3DS is unchanged. Mario Kart 7: 36 dropped
frames in 103 s with both screens; Smash encodes ~2x faster.

Also:
- the version shown on the panel was stale (0.9.11): the objects that
  print it are now rebuilt when APP_VERSION changes;
- help and README: record only the top screen for smoother video in
  extended-memory games.

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: record extended-memory games on Old 3DS (0.9.13 beta)

Games that need 80 MB on an Old 3DS (Smash, Pokemon Sun/Moon and
Ultra, Mario Maker, Monster Hunter) reboot the console when they
start, which ended the recorder. Right before that reboot the
recorder now leaves Rosalina a one-time order to load a tiny launcher
plugin into the game; the plugin starts the recorder again and the
recording goes on in a new file.

The plugin takes its 2 MB from the game's own memory and the recorder
keeps every buffer there, so SYSTEM memory stays as the game left it
and the HOME Menu works as without the recorder. The plugin loader is
turned on just for that game if it was off. Closing such a game saves
the recording and the app explains it afterwards. New 3DS and normal
games are unchanged.

Also: help topic and README section about these games.

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: show the Telegram channel on the help screen

Co-authored-by: Claude Code Agent <noreply@anthropic.com>

pages.html:/repos/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder/r:
3DS Recorder

Record everything on your Nintendo 3DS — games, the HOME Menu and apps, both screens with sound.
Made in Ukraine 🇺🇦

English · Українська

English

What it is

3DS Recorder records the whole console: whatever is on the screens, in any game, the HOME Menu or a system app, with the game sound. Press a button combination to start, press it again to stop — the video is saved to the SD card.

You do not need a PC or a capture card. The console turns each recording into a small MP4 video by itself, and you can send it to your phone over Wi-Fi by scanning a QR code.

[!WARNING] This is a beta (0.11.4). It has been tested on an Old 3DS and a New 3DS XL with Luma3DS 13.5, but not on every console, game and SD card, so bugs are possible. If something goes wrong, please open an issue and attach the log (see Problems and feedback) — every report helps make the release better.

What you need

  • A Nintendo 3DS, 3DS XL, 2DS, New 3DS, New 3DS XL or New 2DS XL with Luma3DS custom firmware.
  • FBI to install the .cia (or the Homebrew Launcher for the .3dsx).
  • Free space on the SD card: up to ~320 MB per minute in 3D games (both screens, 30 fps; menus and 2D games take much less). The MP4 made from it is about 10 MB a minute.
  • To get videos on your phone: the phone and the console on the same Wi-Fi network (the console uses 2.4 GHz).

Install

  1. Download 3ds-recorder.cia (or 3ds-recorder.3dsx) from Releases.
  2. Copy it to the SD card and install the .cia with FBI (the .3dsx goes to /3ds/).
  3. Turn the console on while holding SELECT to open the Luma menu. Turn on Enable loading external FIRMs and modules and save with START.
  4. Open 3DS Recorder, choose your language and read the short guide. The recorder starts by itself: the notification LED glows blue for a moment.

How to use

  • Start / stop a recording: R + SELECT, anywhere — in a game, in the HOME Menu, in an app. You can close 3DS Recorder: the recorder keeps running in the background.
  • The LED tells you what is happening:
    • blue for a moment — the recorder is ready;
    • red, breathing — recording;
    • green twice — the recording is saved;
    • red three times — something went wrong (usually a full SD card); open the app to see why.
  • After each power-on, open 3DS Recorder once — that starts the recorder again.
  • Watch: open the Gallery and press A.
  • Get the video on your phone: in the Gallery press Y on a recording, scan the QR code with the phone's camera and tap Save the video. Nothing to install on the phone; iPhone and Android both work.
  • Or take it from the SD card: recordings are in /3ds/recorder/recordings/. Next to each recording (.r3d) the console makes an .mp4 that plays anywhere.
  • Settings: frame rate (15 / 20 / 30 fps), both screens, the top one or the bottom one only, sound on or off, the LED, the language and the button combination.

Good to know

  • Leaving System Settings, starting a DS or GBA game, or turning the console off restarts the console. The recording is saved and stops there; open 3DS Recorder again afterwards. The app tells you what happened.
  • Closing the lid saves the recording; it goes on in a new file when you open the lid.
  • If the power is cut (battery, crash), the recording is recovered the next time you open the app.
  • Long recordings continue in a new file every 4 GB (a 1–2 second gap): the SD card's FAT32 limit.
  • Fast 3D scenes on a slow SD card may be recorded at a lower frame rate for a moment: the card cannot keep up.
  • DS and GBA games can't be recorded: they run in a separate mode of the console.
  • Games that need extra memory on an Old 3DS (Smash Bros, Pokémon Sun / Moon and Ultra Sun / Ultra Moon, Super Mario Maker, Monster Hunter) restart the console when they start and when they close. If the recorder runs, it comes back inside the game by itself and the recording goes on in a new file: right before the restart it leaves Luma's plugin loader a one-time order to load a tiny launcher plugin (about 1 KB) into that game, which starts the recorder again and does nothing else. If the plugin loader is off, it is turned on for that one game and off again afterwards. The game gets 2 MB less memory, the recorder keeps its buffers in those 2 MB, and the video is less smooth there; recording only the top screen (Settings → Screens → Top) makes it smoother. When such a game closes, the recording is saved; open 3DS Recorder to record again. A New 3DS does not restart for these games.
  • On a New 3DS, the few games that use the 800-pixel wide top screen are recorded at 400 pixels: only the left half.

Remove

Settings → Uninstall recorder. It removes the recorder, its settings and logs, and the app itself. Your recordings stay unless you tick the box. Luma settings are not changed.

Problems and feedback

This is a beta: every report helps. Please open an issue, say what you did and what happened (console model, game), and attach the log: on the phone page (the QR code) tap Log for the developer at the bottom, or copy /3ds/recorder/app.log and recorder.log from the SD card.

Building from source

The recorder is a Luma3DS sysmodule (sysmod/) plus the control app (app/), which carries the sysmodule and the launcher plugin (plugin/) inside. A Docker image with devkitARM, libctru and 3gxtool builds all three:

docker build -t 3dsrec-dev tools/
tools/dkp.sh plugin make          # plugin/rec3ds-launch.3gx
tools/dkp.sh sysmod make          # sysmod/rec3ds.cxi
tools/dkp.sh app make cia         # app/3ds-recorder.cia and .3dsx
Folder What
sysmod/ the recorder: reads the screens and the sound, compresses them (XR32, lossless) and writes .r3d
app/ the app: install, settings, gallery, player, the Wi-Fi server for the phone
plugin/ the launcher plugin for extended-memory games on an Old 3DS (starts the recorder again inside the game)
prep/ turns an .r3d into MP4 (H.264 + AAC) on the console
web/ the page the phone opens
codec/ the screen codecs and the .r3d format
tools/ build helpers, r3dconv / r3d2mp4.sh (.r3d → MP4 on a computer)
tests/ host tests and benchmarks

Thanks

Luma3DS, devkitPro / libctru / citro2d, minih264, vo-aacenc (Apache 2.0), QR Code generator (MIT), mp4-muxer (MIT), Inter font (SIL OFL). Their licenses are next to their code in third_party/, web/vendor/ and app/assets/fonts/.

License

MIT. The third-party parts keep their own licenses (above).

Українська

Що це

3DS Recorder записує всю консоль: усе, що на екранах, у будь-якій грі, меню HOME чи системній програмі, разом зі звуком гри. Натисніть комбінацію кнопок — запис почнеться, ще раз — відео збережеться на SD-картку.

Не потрібні ні комп'ютер, ні карта захоплення. Консоль сама перетворює кожен запис на невелике відео MP4, а забрати його на телефон можна по Wi-Fi, відсканувавши QR-код.

[!WARNING] Це бета-версія (0.11.4). Її перевірено на Old 3DS і New 3DS XL з Luma3DS 13.5, але не на кожній консолі, грі й SD-картці, тож можливі баги. Якщо щось пішло не так, будь ласка, створіть issue і додайте журнал (див. Проблеми і відгуки) — кожен звіт допомагає зробити реліз кращим.

Що потрібно

  • Nintendo 3DS, 3DS XL, 2DS, New 3DS, New 3DS XL або New 2DS XL з кастомною прошивкою Luma3DS.
  • FBI, щоб встановити .cia (або Homebrew Launcher для .3dsx).
  • Вільне місце на SD-картці: до ~320 MB на хвилину у 3D-іграх (обидва екрани, 30 fps; меню і 2D-ігри займають набагато менше). MP4 з такого запису — близько 10 MB на хвилину.
  • Щоб отримати відео на телефон: телефон і консоль в одній Wi-Fi мережі (консоль працює на 2.4 GHz).

Встановлення

  1. Завантажте 3ds-recorder.cia (або 3ds-recorder.3dsx) з Releases.
  2. Скопіюйте на SD-картку і встановіть .cia через FBI (.3dsx кладеться в /3ds/).
  3. Увімкніть консоль із затиснутою SELECT — відкриється меню Luma. Увімкніть Enable loading external FIRMs and modules і збережіть кнопкою START.
  4. Відкрийте 3DS Recorder, виберіть мову і прочитайте короткий гайд. Рекордер запуститься сам: індикатор LED на мить засвітиться синім.

Як користуватися

  • Почати / зупинити запис: R + SELECT будь-де — у грі, в меню HOME, у програмі. 3DS Recorder можна закрити: рекордер працює далі у фоні.
  • LED показує, що відбувається:
    • синій на мить — рекордер готовий;
    • червоний «дихає» — іде запис;
    • зелений двічі — запис збережено;
    • червоний тричі — щось пішло не так (найчастіше заповнена SD-картка); відкрийте додаток, щоб дізнатися причину.
  • Після кожного ввімкнення консолі відкрийте 3DS Recorder один раз — так рекордер запускається знову.
  • Переглянути: відкрийте Галерею і натисніть A.
  • Отримати відео на телефон: у Галереї натисніть Y на записі, відскануйте QR-код камерою телефона і натисніть Зберегти відео. На телефон нічого ставити не треба; працює і на iPhone, і на Android.
  • Або забрати з SD-картки: записи лежать у /3ds/recorder/recordings/. Поруч із кожним записом (.r3d) консоль робить .mp4, яке відтворюється будь-де.
  • Налаштування: частота кадрів (15 / 20 / 30 fps), обидва екрани, лише верхній чи лише нижній, звук, LED, мова і комбінація кнопок.

Варто знати

  • Вихід з Налаштувань консолі, запуск DS- чи GBA-гри або вимкнення перезапускають консоль. Запис на цьому зберігається і зупиняється; потім знову відкрийте 3DS Recorder. Додаток пояснить, що сталося.
  • Закрита кришка зберігає запис, а після відкриття він продовжується новим файлом.
  • Якщо зникло живлення (батарея, збій), запис відновиться, коли ви наступного разу відкриєте додаток.
  • Довгі записи продовжуються в новому файлі кожні 4 GB (пауза 1–2 секунди): це обмеження FAT32 на SD-картці.
  • Швидкі 3D-сцени на повільній SD-картці можуть на мить записатися з меншою частотою кадрів: картка не встигає.
  • DS- і GBA-ігри записати не можна: вони працюють в окремому режимі консолі.
  • Ігри, яким на Old 3DS треба більше пам'яті (Smash Bros, Pokémon Sun / Moon і Ultra Sun / Ultra Moon, Super Mario Maker, Monster Hunter), перезапускають консоль, коли стартують і коли закриваються. Якщо рекордер працює, він сам повертається в гру, а запис продовжується новим файлом: перед перезапуском він залишає завантажувачу плагінів Luma одноразову інструкцію завантажити в цю гру крихітний плагін-запускач (близько 1 КБ), який лише знову запускає рекордер. Якщо завантажувач плагінів вимкнено, він вмикається лише на цю гру і потім вимикається. Грі лишається на 2 МБ менше пам'яті, рекордер тримає свої буфери в цих 2 МБ, і відео там менш плавне; запис лише верхнього екрана (Налаштування → Екрани → Верхній) робить його плавнішим. Коли така гра закривається, запис зберігається; щоб писати далі, відкрийте 3DS Recorder. New 3DS для цих ігор не перезапускається.
  • На New 3DS кілька ігор із широким верхнім екраном 800 пікселів записуються у 400 пікселях: лише ліва половина.

Видалення

Налаштування → Видалити рекордер. Видаляє рекордер, його налаштування й журнали та сам додаток. Записи лишаються, якщо не поставити позначку. Налаштування Luma не змінюються.

Проблеми і відгуки

Це бета: кожен звіт допомагає. Будь ласка, створіть issue, напишіть, що робили і що сталося (модель консолі, гра), і додайте журнал: на сторінці в телефоні (через QR-код) унизу натисніть Журнал для розробника, або скопіюйте з SD-картки /3ds/recorder/app.log і recorder.log.

Збірка з кодів

Рекордер — це sysmodule для Luma3DS (sysmod/) і додаток керування (app/), який несе sysmodule в собі. Обидва збираються в Docker-образі з devkitARM і libctru — команди й опис тек у розділі Building from source.

Подяки

Luma3DS, devkitPro / libctru / citro2d, minih264, vo-aacenc (Apache 2.0), QR Code generator (MIT), mp4-muxer (MIT), шрифт Inter (SIL OFL). Їхні ліцензії лежать поруч з їхнім кодом у third_party/, web/vendor/ і app/assets/fonts/.

Ліцензія

MIT. Сторонні частини мають власні ліцензії (див. вище).

Зроблено в Україні 🇺🇦

json:/repos/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder/r.name: 3DS Recorder 0.11.4 beta
json:/repos/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder/r.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Beta.** Tested on an Old 3DS with Luma3DS 13.5. The New 3DS changes in this release (faster processor while recording, new compression, 800 px mode) have not been tested on a New 3DS yet. If something goes wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder/issues/new) and attach the log (phone page → **Log for the developer**, or `/3ds/recorder/app.log` and `recorder.log` from the SD card).

## What's new in 0.11.4

- **Both screens stay smooth when the SD card is the limit.** In 3D games the card can't take every frame of both screens. The bottom screen used to pause then; now it slows down a little first and the top keeps its full rate. Mario Kart 7 on an Old 3DS: about 22 fps on top and 11 below, steady, with no lost frames.
- **Better sound:** the recorder now sleeps between frames instead of waking up every 2 ms, which leaves the system core to the game. The longest gap in sound polling went from about 0.2 s to under 7 ms.
- **Faster SD writes** (bigger write blocks, the recorder's SD access at low priority so the game's own loading comes first) and less wasted space in recordings.
- **Settings → Screens → Bottom:** record only the bottom screen, for games played there.
- **Games that need extra memory on an Old 3DS** (Smash, Pokémon Sun / Moon…): about 9% more of the SD bandwidth goes to the video.
- **New 3DS:** the processor runs at 804 MHz with the L2 cache while recording (back as it was afterwards), frames that change all over are compressed much better, a bigger buffer rides out slow SD cards, and games using the 800 px top screen mode are recorded whole.
- **Fixed:** the console could crash when a recording was started in the HOME Menu and a game was then launched.
- The free-space estimate is realistic now: up to ~320 MB a minute in 3D games (the MP4 for the phone is still about 10 MB a minute).

Recordings made by older versions still play and convert. Recordings made by 0.11 need 0.11 or newer to play.

**Install:** `3ds-recorder.cia` with FBI (or `3ds-recorder.3dsx` in `/3ds/` for the Homebrew Launcher). In the Luma menu (hold SELECT at power-on) turn on **Enable loading external FIRMs and modules**. Open 3DS Recorder; **R + SELECT** starts and stops a recording. Updating: install over the old version and open the app once. Details: [README](https://github.com/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder#english).

---

> **Бета.** Перевірено на Old 3DS з Luma3DS 13.5. Зміни для New 3DS у цьому релізі (швидший процесор під час запису, нове стиснення, режим 800 px) ще не перевірені на New 3DS. Якщо щось пішло не так, будь ласка, [створіть issue](https://github.com/BolgarMaxym97/3ds-recorder/issues/new) і додайте журнал (сторінка в телефоні → **Журнал для розробника**, або `/3ds/recorder/app.log` і `recorder.log` з SD-картки).

## Що нового в 0.11.4

- **Обидва екрани плавні, навіть коли межа — SD-картка.** У 3D-іграх картка не встигає за кожним кадром обох екранів. Раніше тоді зупинявся нижній екран; тепер він спершу трохи сповільнюється, а верхній лишається на повній частоті. Mario Kart 7 на Old 3DS: близько 22 fps зверху і 11 знизу, рівно, без втрачених кадрів.
- **Кращий звук:** рекордер тепер спить між кадрами, а не прокидається кожні 2 мс, і лишає системне ядро грі. Найдовша пауза в опитуванні звуку — менше 7 мс замість ~0.2 с.
- **Швидший запис на SD** (більші блоки, доступ рекордера до SD з низьким пріоритетом, щоб завантаження гри йшло першим) і менше зайвого місця в записах.
- **Налаштування → Екрани → Нижній:** запис лише нижнього екрана, для ігор, у які грають на ньому.
- **Ігри, яким на Old 3DS треба більше пам'яті** (Smash, Pokémon Sun / Moon…): відео отримує приблизно на 9% більше пропускної здатності SD.
- **New 3DS:** під час запису процесор працює на 804 МГц з кешем L2 (після запису — як було), кадри, що змінюються повністю, стискаються значно краще, більший буфер переживає повільні SD-картки, а ігри з режимом верхнього екрана 800 px записуються повністю.
- **Виправлено:** консоль могла падати, якщо запис почати в меню HOME, а потім запустити гру.

What's new in 0.11.4

  • Both screens stay smooth when the SD card is the limit. In 3D games the card can't take every frame of both screens. The bottom screen used to pause then; now it slows down a little first and the top keeps its full rate. Mario Kart 7 on an Old 3DS: about 22 fps on top and 11 below, steady, with no lost frames.
  • Better sound: the recorder now sleeps between frames instead of waking up every 2 ms, which leaves the system core to the game. The longest gap in sound polling went from about 0.2 s to under 7 ms.
  • Faster SD writes (bigger write blocks, the recorder's SD access at low priority so the game's own loading comes first) and less wasted space in recordings.
  • Settings → Screens → Bottom: record only the bottom screen, for games played there.
  • Games that need extra memory on an Old 3DS (Smash, Pokémon Sun / Moon…): about 9% more of the SD bandwidth goes to the video.
  • New 3DS: the processor runs at 804 MHz with the L2 cache while recording (back as it was afterwards), frames that change all over are compressed much better, a bigger buffer rides out slow SD cards, and games using the 800 px top screen mode are recorded whole.
  • Fixed: the console could crash when a recording was started in the HOME Menu and a game was then launched.
  • The free-space estimate is realistic now: up to ~320 MB a minute in 3D games (the MP4 for the phone is still about 10 MB a minute).

Recordings made by older versions still play and convert. Recordings made by 0.11 need 0.11 or newer to play.

Install: 3ds-recorder.cia with FBI (or 3ds-recorder.3dsx in /3ds/ for the Homebrew Launcher). In the Luma menu (hold SELECT at power-on) turn on Enable loading external FIRMs and modules. pages.html:/repos/BreadChaser/PSX3D/readme:
PSX3D

A PlayStation emulator built for the Nintendo 3DS.
GPU rendering, a box-art library and recommended settings for a growing list of games.

Install · Controls · Performance · FAQ · Report a problem


Main menu
Library
Crash Bandicoot on Old 3DS

PSX3D plays PlayStation games on every 3DS and 2DS. It draws with the 3DS graphics chip, puts your library one tap away, and applies recommended settings for a growing list of tested games (US editions so far). No BIOS file needed.

[!NOTE] PSX3D is a work in progress and improves with every release. Most games run well; demanding 3D games run slower on the Old 3DS. See Performance and Known issues.

[!TIP] Coming next: BreadBox, a multi-system emulator for the 3DS built on PSX3D, starting with PlayStation and Game Boy Advance.

Features

Plays well

  • Hardware (GPU) rendering on Old and New 3DS
  • Tested settings per game and per console, applied automatically
  • Auto frameskip that keeps games at full speed where it can
  • Widescreen in games with a tested widescreen fix
  • Fast forward in every game
  • Built-in BIOS: a BIOS file is optional

Easy to use

  • Main menu with Continue: back in your game in one press
  • Box-art library with recently played games, favorites, sorting and a letter jump
  • Box art downloads by itself; clean titles; multi-disc games grouped
  • Finds your games on the SD card without any setup
  • Twelve animated color themes with a live preview in Settings → Display → Theme
  • Theme-colored menu icons and in-game touch controls

Keeps your progress safe

  • Your place is saved when you quit, when the 3DS sleeps and every few minutes
  • Save states with previews
  • The last ten automatic saves and dated memory card copies are kept per game
  • Undo in the pause menu takes back the last load, save or reset

And more

  • Cheats, disc swapping, remappable buttons
  • Touch-screen L2/R2 for the Old 3DS, plus a right stick in analog games

New 3DS extras

  • 3D: raise the 3D slider and the picture sits behind the screen. Real 3D (experimental, Settings → Display → 3D) gives every object its own depth; it slows busy scenes.
  • Rewind: hold SELECT + L to go back a few seconds.
  • Faster PS1 processor for games that slowed down on a real PlayStation (Crash Team Racing, Gran Turismo 2, Silent Hill, Need for Speed: High Stakes).

Install

You need a 3DS or 2DS with Luma3DS custom firmware, and your own PlayStation game images.

  1. Open FBI → Remote Install → Scan QR Code and scan this code:

    Or download PSX3D.cia and install it with FBI.

  2. Copy your games to sdmc:/roms/psx/.

  3. Start PSX3D from the HOME Menu.

To update, scan the same code again. A .3dsx for the Homebrew Launcher is on the release page.

Getting started

Games. PSX3D reads .cue/.bin, .chd, .pbp, .iso, .img, .mdf and .m3u. It looks in sdmc:/roms/psx/ and other common folders; to use another folder, pick it in Settings → Games folder. Press SELECT in the library to scan again after adding games.

Box art downloads automatically, even for files with unusual names. To use your own picture, see box art.

BIOS. Not needed. If you have a real PlayStation BIOS, copy it to sdmc:/3ds/PSX3D/bios/ and PSX3D uses it (scph5500.bin, scph5501.bin, scph5502.bin, scph1001.bin, scph7001.bin, scph101.bin or psxonpsp660.bin).

Your files live in sdmc:/3ds/PSX3D/:

Folder or file What it holds
saves/ Memory cards
states/ Save states and Continue
backups/ Save backups
config.ini, games/ Your settings
log.txt What happened last session (older ones: log.1.txt to log.4.txt)

Controls

Where Button Action
Main menu A / X Open / Settings
Library A / X / Y Play / Sort / Favorite
Library L / R Previous / next letter
Library SELECT Scan for new games
In game A / B / X / Y Circle / Cross / Triangle / Square
In game L / R / ZL / ZR L1 / R1 / L2 / R2
In game Circle Pad / C-Stick D-pad or left stick / right stick
In game Tap MENU (touch screen) Pause menu
In game SELECT + R Fast forward on / off
In game Hold SELECT + L Rewind (New 3DS)

Every button and both shortcuts can be changed in Settings → Controls. The Old 3DS shows L2 and R2 on the touch screen, plus a right stick in analog games.

Settings

Settings has four pages: Display, Controls, Saves and Advanced. Open it from the main menu to change all games, or from the pause menu to change only the game you are playing. Tested games already start with the best values for your console, so most players never need Advanced. Reset this game and Reset all settings put everything back.

Performance

PSX3D is tuned hardest for the Old 3DS. Most games run at or near full speed with Auto frameskip; demanding 3D games, such as racing games, run slower.

Exact numbers

Old 3DS, heaviest tested scene of each game. Speed: 100% = full speed. Most PS1 3D games run at 30 FPS at most; Symphony of the Night, Tekken 3 and Klonoa at 60. See methodology and compatibility.

Game (Old 3DS) Frameskip off: speed / FPS Auto frameskip: speed / FPS
Crash Bandicoot 91.2% / 22.1 98.4% / 17.1
Crash Bandicoot 2 85.4% / 26.0 98.2% / 17.3
Crash Team Racing 80.8% / 23.9 91.7% / 15.1
Gran Turismo 2 58.0% / 15.0 58.3% / 13.3
Ridge Racer Type 4 85.0% / 25.8 91.9% / 18.7
Need for Speed: High Stakes 37.2% / 11.9 37.5% / 10.9
Tekken 3 69.6% / 42.3 95.6% / 15.2
Final Fantasy VII 99.9% / 15.1 99.9% / 15.2
Klonoa 91.3% / 55.2 100.0% / 15.2
Silent Hill (alley) 76.8% / 23.3 90.5% / 15.2
Silent Hill (café) 80.1% / 18.9 86.7% / 15.2
Symphony of the Night 100.1% / 60.6 100.0% / 56.8

New 3DS: every game above runs at full speed in its heaviest tested scene with Auto frameskip.

Known issues

  • Some games show drawing glitches, flicker or thin cracks at polygon edges.
  • Demanding 3D games run below full speed on the Old 3DS.
  • Real 3D (New 3DS) is experimental and slows busy scenes.
  • European discs with LibCrypt protection need a matching .sbi file next to the disc image (details).
  • With the built-in BIOS, the first Gran Turismo hangs and Mega Man Legends 2 goes black after the intro. A real BIOS fixes Gran Turismo.

Found something else? Open an issue and attach log.txt if you can.

Planned features

  • Play together: play with a friend over local wireless. Both players with their own copy of the game, or stream the game to a friend who doesn't have it.
  • Join through Download Play: a friend's 3DS gets PSX3D's join app straight from the Download Play menu.
  • Better Real 3D: full speed and more depth in more games.
  • More tuned games: recommended settings for more of the PlayStation library on both consoles.
  • BreadBox: PSX3D's approach for more systems, starting with PlayStation and Game Boy Advance.

FAQ

Old 3DS or New 3DS? Both are supported. The New 3DS runs the games in the performance table at full speed with Auto frameskip, and adds 3D, rewind and a faster PS1 processor. The Old 3DS runs most games well; demanding 3D games are slower there.

Which game files work? .cue/.bin, .chd, .pbp, .iso, .img, .mdf and .m3u for multi-disc games. .ccd (CloneCD) images don't load; convert them to .cue/.bin or .chd.

Why is it slow in Azahar or without Luma3DS? PSX3D's fast mode needs Luma3DS on a real console. Without it PSX3D still starts, but much slower.

Do I need a BIOS? No. A BIOS is built in. A real one is used automatically if you add it.

Building from source

You need devkitPro (devkitARM, libctru, citro2d, citro3d), makerom and bannertool. Full steps are in docs/building.md.

git clone https://github.com/BreadChaser/PSX3D.git
cd PSX3D
make        # psx3d/PSX3D.3dsx
make cia    # psx3d/PSX3D.cia

Credits and licence

  • BreadChaser: PSX3D
  • PCSX-ReARMed: notaz, Exophase and libretro contributors; based on PCSX, PCSX-Reloaded and P.E.Op.S.
  • The PCSX-ReARMed 3DS port authors; devkitPro (libctru, citro2d, citro3d)
  • DSP1 by zoogie; artwork, fonts and cheat sources
  • Icons by Dreamstale from Flaticon (Flaticon licence, not GPL)

PSX3D is licensed under the GPL-2.0. It is not affiliated with Sony, Nintendo or libretro.

Older version — get the latest from the [latest release](https://github.com/BreadChaser/PSX3D/releases/latest).

## Highlights

- **Old 3DS, busy scenes** (game speed, frameskip off): Crash Bandicoot 2 48% → 70%, Crash Team Racing 59% → 75%, Tekken 3 53% → 64%, Silent Hill 60% → 67–68%; Ridge Racer Type 4, Gran Turismo 2 and Need for Speed: High Stakes about 10% faster.
- **New 3DS:** every tested heavy scene runs at full speed, now including Need for Speed: High Stakes.
- **Fixed:** HOME → Close froze on the "Closing software" screen (GitHub issue #1); closing now takes about a second and still saves your place.
- **Fixed a New 3DS crash** in very busy start-ups (Crash Bandicoot 2's intro; openings of Metal Gear Solid, Grandia and Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee).
- **Texture cache no longer thrashes:** Ridge Racer Type 4 races on Old 3DS 33% → 78%; Need for Speed: High Stakes on New 3DS 48% → full speed.
- **Klonoa about 45% faster on Old 3DS** (58% → 84%, 98% with Auto) by skipping the game's repeated "has the next frame started" checks.
- **Crash Bandicoot about 3% faster on Old 3DS** by skipping its wait loop the same way.
- **Faster PS1 emulation on Old 3DS** through quicker scratchpad and memory access.
- **Real widescreen** for 22 games with a tested fix (20 on Old 3DS); games without a fix offer only 4:3 and Stretch.
- **Gran Turismo 2 on Old 3DS** offers Widescreen with a warning that it can lower the speed (about 2% in a busy race, 4–6% in a lighter scene).
- **Cleaner menus:** per-game settings when opened in a game, help text on the top screen, a new folder browser, Cheats only in the pause menu.
- **Dithering on by default,** like a real PlayStation: no more colour bands in Silent Hill's fog.
- **Fixed** the thin blue line at the top of Crash Bandicoot's picture.
- "Continue where I left off" is always on; logs keep the last five sessions.
- Old 3DS numbers above were measured while it streamed its screen over Wi-Fi, which costs 1–3%.

## Known issues

- The GPU renderer still has drawing errors and missing effects.
- Stereoscopic 3D is still unavailable (the 3D slider shows a flat picture).
- Rewind requires New 3DS.
- No display centering or interlaced modes.
- Heavy Wi-Fi traffic and slow cover downloads can cause audio clicks.

  • Automatic box art on both console models, with lower memory use.
  • Built-in HLE BIOS: add your games and play without a separate BIOS file.
  • Safer HLE memory-card saves: fixes corruption when creating multi-block files.
  • FPS display shows new pictures per second alongside game speed.
  • Faster scratchpad access, indirect-block lookup and geometry calculations.
  • Fixes for movie synchronization, border clearing and corrupted menus after leaving a game.
  • Optional developer tools for input recording and replay.

Known issues

  • The GPU renderer is experimental: incorrect effects, flicker and other drawing errors; a thin blue line at the top of Crash Bandicoot's picture.
  • Stereoscopic 3D is unavailable (the 3D slider shows a flat picture).
  • Cheats appear both in the pause menu and in Settings.
  • Rewind requires New 3DS.
  • No display centering or interlaced modes.
  • Heavy Wi-Fi traffic and slow cover downloads can cause audio clicks.
