Mario Kart Wii 3DS Redux

A native Nintendo 3DS port of Mario Kart Wii, based on dudewhat's original port and MiniBandit's continuation.

Features

  • Grand Prix with 50cc, 100cc, 150cc and Mirror classes, cup progression, unlocks and award ceremonies.
  • Time Trials with saved records, solo and team VS, and Balloon Battle and Coin Runners.
  • Character and vehicle selection, including unlockable vehicles and native 3DS Mii drivers.
  • Four license slots with saved identities, rules, records and presentation settings.
  • Dual-screen menus, race results and maps, with restored model materials, animations, particles and audio.
  • Optional dynamic shadows.
  • Notification LED effects for items, race events and drifting, with mode and brightness settings.
  • Distance-based opponent detail and adaptive animation updates for demanding scenes.

See CHANGELOG.md for the full cumulative change list. Online play is not included. Performance varies by hardware and course. Target 60; running in the 40–60 range.

What you need

  • Your own Mario Kart Wii USA disc image, game ID RMCE01, in ISO or WBFS format; convert RVZ or NKit images to a supported format first.
  • Your own native 3DS Mii resource file, CFL_Res.dat, obtained separately.
  • devkitARM and libctru, plus picasso, 3dsxtool and tex3ds.
  • Python 3, Node.js, npm, Git, ffmpeg and a host C/C++ compiler for offline utilities.
  • The converter dependencies and revisions listed in dependencies.json and vendor/sources.lock.json.
  • makerom and bannertool for CIA work, plus a banner model generated from your disc; the icon, logo PNGs and banner sound are included.
  • A separate working directory for extracted files, converted resources and compiler outputs, with room for both the disc and its intermediates.

Patched Kinoko, Citro3D and CFL source is included. Acquire the remaining converter dependencies yourself and apply the relevant files in patches/. The repository includes eight MK7 marker images inherited from the original project and the supplied HOME icon and logo; other game assets, native Mii system resources, generated game headers, saves and compiled packages are not supplied.

Building

Building is manual. Banner-only tools are documented in HOME-BANNER.md. The steps below describe the order; the linked references provide the conversion stages, source list and compiler settings. They are intended for developers comfortable with the 3DS toolchain, not as a one-command build recipe.

1. Prepare the tools

Install the SDK and utilities listed above, and obtain the external converter checkouts at their pinned revisions. Populate vendor/gclib before installing the Python requirements, since it is an editable local dependency. Set up a Python environment and install the listed packages:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund

Use the Windows activation command if working in a Windows shell. Paths in the examples below are placeholders and must be replaced with your own.

2. Extract your disc and convert the resources

Inspect the disc inventory, then extract the files needed by each stage:

python3 tools/extract_disc.py /external/RMCE01.iso /external/extracted --list-only
python3 tools/extract_disc.py /external/RMCE01.iso /external/extracted --prefix Scene/

Follow the resource-stage reference and manual resource instructions for courses, characters, vehicles, menus, movies, audio and effects. Each resource family is a separate operation; there is no full-course or full-roster scheduler.

For example, bundle one exporter, export one BRRES model, then convert it:

node tools/bundle_cooker.mjs tools/export_brres.ts
node build/export_brres.mjs /external/source.brres /external/exported ModelName
python3 tools/cook_model.py /external/exported /external/cooked --prefix model_name

Some converters retain the original data/, assets/, build/ and sd-card/ path conventions; inspect their inputs before running them and keep generated content out of the published source tree. A Wii disc does not supply the native 3DS CFL_Res.dat file.

3. Prepare archives and generated headers

Create the runtime file map, review its paths and pack the resources explicitly:

python3 tools/resource_manifest.py > /external/runtime-files.json
python3 tools/pack_race_assets.py /external/runtime-files.json /external/race.pak --exclude-menu /external/menu.pak

Prepare menu.pak first with pack_menu_assets.py; apply the LOD and Mii archive overlays separately. Keep metadata read outside the archives at its required loose path. See archive preparation.

Produce the 66 external headers declared in config/generated-inputs.json, then provide their directory as a compiler include path. The approved Bowser's Castle visibility policy is already included in include/mkw/castle_regions.hpp; a normal build does not need a browser bake.

4. Compile the libraries and game

Prepare the shader headers with picasso, compile the bundled Citro3D and CFL sources, and archive those objects. Then compile the game translation units listed in MANUAL-PROGRAM-SOURCES.txt.

Use the exact architecture flags, include paths and linker wrappers in the compilation instructions and library flags. Application sources use GNU C++23; Kinoko sources additionally use LTO. Do not enable fast-math or MKW_FRAME_CAPTURE for a normal release.

After linking the ELF, create the homebrew executable:

3dsxtool /external/mkw-3ds.elf /external/mkw-3ds.3dsx

5. Package a CIA, if needed

Follow HOME banner preparation for the included artwork and the explicit extraction, scene and CGFX conversion stages. The approved banner audio is included; see that document for current verification limits. Prepare the SMDH and banner with bannertool. Copy the RSF template to your working directory and remove its RomFs block for an external-SD build. Then invoke makerom with your compiled ELF and prepared HOME assets:

makerom -f cia -target t -exefslogo -elf /external/mkw-3ds.elf -rsf /external/external-sd.rsf -icon /external/icon.icn -banner /external/banner.bnr -ver 148 -DAPP_REMASTER=0 -o /external/MKW-3DS-v0.9.4.cia

Version 0.9.4 uses title version 148. Check the resulting Ticket/TMD version and contents; some makerom builds have a version-macro collision described in the packaging notes.

Installing and running

Place the converted runtime files under sd:/3ds/mkw-3ds/, including menu.pak, race.pak and the loose files required by the resource map.

  • Homebrew: place mkw-3ds.3dsx in that directory and launch it with the Homebrew Launcher.
  • CIA: install the CIA with your console's title installer and retain the runtime resources on the SD card.
  • Emulator: launch the 3DSX in Azahar with its emulated SD directory pointing to the staged resource tree and the required system data configured.

On hardware, dump your DSP firmware with DSP1 if it is not already available. Do not copy an emulator-only DSP stub to a console. When updating, preserve rksys.dat, its backup, license-options-*.dat, last-license.txt and mii-*.3dsmii. Game resources and personal system data are not part of the source release.

Controls

Button Action
Circle Pad Steer and choose the direction of an item throw
A Accelerate
B Brake / reverse
R Hop and drift; trick off a ramp
Y / D-pad Up Trick / bike wheelie
X / ZL Look behind
L Use item
D-pad / ZR Boost panel trick
START Pause
SELECT Toggle the speedometer
Touch screen Switch the bottom-screen map view

Dynamic shadows and LED options are in License Settings.

Contributing

Include the hardware or emulator used, the game mode, course and steps to reproduce a problem. Distinguish build checks from gameplay testing. Keep game assets, generated files, saves and native system resources out of source changes, and preserve third-party license notices.

Credits

  • dudewhat - original Mario Kart Wii 3DS port.
  • MiniBandit - the continuation this project builds on.
  • Epic - Redux development and integration.
  • DarthMDev: Old 3DS drawing performance fix, race sound fixes and menu cadence
  • Codiak540: Old 3DS performance testing and optimisation research (course-object detail distance, particle limit, performance log idea)
  • janedoemk3ds: Old 3DS performance research with Codiak540 (lighter models, visibility culling, faster course drawing; PR #40 in repo mkw-3ds)
  • vabold / Kinoko - Mario Kart Wii physics.
  • noclip.website - BRRES model parsing.
  • LagoLunatic / gclib - disc and texture utilities.
  • devkitPro, libctru and Citro3D - Nintendo 3DS development and graphics libraries.
  • CFL contributors - native Mii rendering support.
  • ogws and mkw decompilation projects - original-behavior references.
  • Project CTR / makerom and bannertool contributors - packaging tools.

See LICENSE, NOTICE and licenses/ for attribution and licensing, including unresolved original-port and CFL license scopes; the root MIT text does not cover the whole snapshot. Mario Kart Wii is copyright Nintendo; this is an unofficial fan project and is not affiliated with Nintendo.

pages.html:/repos/EstebanPdN/dusklight-3ds/rea:
DuskLight 3DS

Twilight Princess. A native New Nintendo 3DS project.
Experimental source port based on Dusklight.

Status · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Contribute · Community

Native New Nintendo 3DS port work for The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, based on Dusklight and the Twilight Princess decompilation.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex. Learn more about the development process here.

Experimental source publication in active development. No release or playable binary is published. The goal is a complete native port; full-game progression, reliable save/reload and physical New3DS performance remain under development. The new renderer and its game integration are work in progress; the current native model route is not a playable build. See the native renderer roadmap.

Features

Native ARM game integration
Original game and JSystem code linked through a dedicated 3DS platform target.		 Native PICA200 renderer in development
Prepared geometry, shaders, materials and textures submitted directly through Citro3D; whole-game migration remains incomplete.
3DS platform services
Circle Pad and C-Stick mapping, NDSP audio, SD data access and application diagnostics.		 Inspectable development
Source, synthetic host tests, pinned dependencies and maintained build and architecture guides.

These are implemented development systems, with the validation limits described in Compatibility. The 400×240, 2D, 30 Hz target is a goal; sustained 30 FPS on physical hardware has not been established.

Project status

This repository publishes the current source. There is no GitHub release, prerelease, installation QR or supported end-user download. Build instructions are available for developers in Building.

The port targets New Nintendo 3DS, New Nintendo 3DS XL and New Nintendo 2DS XL. Old Nintendo 3DS and Old Nintendo 2DS are outside the current target.

A user-supplied GameCube USA or European/PAL revision 0 game image (GZ2E01 or GZ2P01) is required for runtime data preparation. No disc image, extracted game data, save or private memory capture is included. See Game data.

Documentation

Guide Purpose
Documentation index Start with the guide for your task.
Repository map Source ownership, directory layout and maintenance rules.
Building Toolchain, clean checkout, diagnostic and full integration builds.
Native renderer Current implementation, ten-step roadmap, build/test commands and open gates.
Architecture Engine boundary, rendering, audio, storage and lifecycle.
Compatibility Target systems, implemented paths and remaining acceptance gates.
Game data and controls Local data preparation, SD paths, save format and input mapping.
Configuration CMake options, profiles and experiment boundaries.
Testing Synthetic host checks, target compilation and runtime evidence.
Diagnostics Local reports, dump verification and useful bug reports.
Verification status Checks performed for this source publication.
Source provenance Upstream pins, vendored changes and attribution.

Development

git clone https://github.com/EstebanPdN/dusklight-3ds.git
cd dusklight-3ds
python3 Tools/3ds/check_publication.py
python3 Tools/3ds/test_public_host.py

The source and pinned dependencies are included as ordinary files; a recursive submodule download is not required. Host checks use Python 3 and a C++20 compiler with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. A target build also needs devkitARM, libctru, Citro3D, CMake and the devkitPro 3DS tools.

Build the native integration locally 
export DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro
export DEVKITARM="$DEVKITPRO/devkitARM"
python3 Tools/3ds/build_public.py --profile game

Outputs stay in Build/public-game/. Building does not upload anything or create a release. See Building for the diagnostic profile, exact configuration, prerequisites and current limitations.

Community and bug reports

Join the project Discord for discussion and open a GitHub issue for a reproducible source problem. Include the commit, build profile, toolchain, console or emulator version and concise reproduction steps. See Diagnostics before sharing captures.

Credits

  • Twilit Realm and Dusklight contributors — upstream reimplementation.
  • zeldaret/tp and the GameCube/Wii decompilation community — reconstructed engine and research.
  • Aurora contributors — GX compatibility and native integration foundations.
  • devkitPro — devkitARM, libctru and Citro3D.
  • Cellenseres / OpenDSP — open-source NDSP component.
  • Esteban PDN — New Nintendo 3DS adaptation, project artwork and maintenance, with help from Codex.
  • Nintendo — the original game and its associated names and content.

Full dependency scope is in Third-party notices. This is an independent fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo or Twilit Realm. Upstream project links identify the original authors; the 3DS adaptation and its development process are maintained independently.

License and legal notice

Dusklight and original port contributions follow the upstream CC0 1.0 dedication. Dependencies retain their own licenses and notices; the root dedication does not relicense them or Nintendo game content. See Third-party notices and Artwork.

forge.store

Esteban’s Forge. On your Nintendo 3DS.
A native homebrew storefront and its web design reference, made for two small screens.

Download · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Contribute · Community

Development build, published directly in this repository. No GitHub release has been created. The application targets Old and New Nintendo 3DS. Automated tests and emulator checks are recorded in Verification; physical-console HOME/sleep, installation, launch and sustained audio/video performance still need confirmation.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

Download and installation

Format Download Where it goes
CIA forge-store.cia Install with FBI to the HOME Menu.
3DSX forge-store.3dsx Copy to /3ds/forge-store/ and open in Homebrew Launcher.
Integrity SHA256SUMS · build manifest Verify the downloaded file before installing.

On first entering the store, the app automatically downloads the 16.04 MB Store resources package in the background. Downloads shows one package with combined progress. Each video becomes playable after its own file passes SHA-256 verification; navigation remains available. No account or token is needed. See Installation for controls and cache management.

Every launch checks for a store update before the introduction. When a newer build is found, the touch screen shows its version: Yes downloads and installs it; No fades to black and closes the store. An unavailable check continues to the introduction. Builds without the updater need one manual update first. Public GitHub pages and common images are also cached and refreshed in the background. See Updates and cache.

Game installations are separate from this package. Some ports require files supplied by the player; no ROMs, game data archives, DSP firmware, saves or memory dumps are included here.

Features

Built for two screens
400 × 240 top screen, 320 × 240 touch screen, crisp type, shared tab animations, light and dark themes, and eight interface languages.		 Browse the Forge
Curated ports and community apps, search, layered banners, screenshots, trailers, requirements and release history.
Install and manage
Download queue, staged installs, integrity checks, supported rollback, SD browser, requirement detection, uninstall and application launch.		 Resources that stay ready
Small native-resolution videos, verified persistent cache, automatic background downloads, explicit retry and asynchronous cache cleanup.
Read without leaving
A native GitHub reader for READMEs, releases, images and repository information. Optional Universal-DB integration.		 One visual reference
The web V2 design shares catalog, art, sound and layout decisions with the C application. Original web V1 is preserved.

The web reference uses a simulated SD card and installer. Native installs use the console’s real filesystem and services. Visual parity is an ongoing measured target, not a claim that every state or every GitHub document renders identically.

Run the web reference

Requires Python 3. No npm install or web build is needed.

python3 tools/serve.py 8642

Open http://localhost:8642. Use Resolución 3DS for native resolution and the pixel magnifier to inspect both screens. Keyboard controls follow Azahar: arrows, A/Enter, S/Esc for B, Q/W for L/R, Z for X, X for Y, M for START and N for SELECT. See Web reference. The preserved V1 is at versions/v1/.

Build the application

Install devkitARM, libctru, Citro2D/Citro3D, the documented 3DS portlibs, CMake, Python 3 and zsh. The reviewed RomFS assets are included, so a normal build needs no browser, HandBrake, proprietary game files or access to another project.

zsh 3ds/build.sh

Outputs go to 3ds/build/. The default build disables RAM/VRAM dumps and has no dump-upload endpoint. Use FORGE_DEBUG=1 only for local testing. Read Building for dependencies, asset generation and test commands.

Documentation

  • Documentation index — installation, architecture, media and maintenance.
  • Architecture — module ownership, data flow and thread lifetimes.
  • Media pipeline — HandBrake encoding, format, download contract and verification.
  • Updates and cache — startup updates, incremental GitHub requests and prefetch.
  • Verification — what was tested and what still needs hardware.
  • Asset credits · Third-party notices.
  • Contributing · Security · Changelog.

Community and bug reports

Use GitHub Issues or join Discord. Include the build hash, console model, CIA/3DSX format and steps to reproduce. Do not attach RAM/VRAM dumps, tokens, ROMs or personal SD contents to a public report.

License and legal notice

Rights and licenses are component-specific. Third-party software keeps its original license. Game imagery and trademarks belong to their respective owners; attribution is not a grant of reuse rights. This is an unofficial homebrew project, unaffiliated with Nintendo.

Legend of Doom 3DS

Explore Hyrule from a new perspective.
The Legend of Zelda meets first-person adventure on New Nintendo 3DS.

Download · Features · Documentation · Community

Nintendo 3DS port of Legend of Doom, the first-person GZDoom conversion of the original The Legend of Zelda created by DeTwelve Games.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

v1.0 is available now for New Nintendo 3DS, New Nintendo 3DS XL and New Nintendo 2DS XL. Old Nintendo 3DS, Old Nintendo 3DS XL and Nintendo 2DS are not supported.

The port uses GZDoom 4.7.1 and Freedoom: Phase 2. No NES ROM or commercial Doom IWAD is required.

Download and installation

Stable: v1.0.

Download the published packages from GitHub Releases.

v1.0 download Use
CIA Install with FBI. Includes the matching game and engine data.
Homebrew Launcher ZIP Includes the 3DSX and the SD data folder.
Build manifest / SHA-256 checksums Build identity, component revisions and file verification.

CIA / FBI

Install the CIA with FBI, or open Remote Install → Scan QR Code and scan:

The CIA contains its game data. Configuration, saves and diagnostic files are stored separately under sdmc:/3ds/legend-of-doom/.

Homebrew Launcher / 3DSX

  1. Extract the v1.0 ZIP.
  2. Copy its included 3ds folder to the root of the SD card.
  3. Launch sdmc:/3ds/legend-of-doom/legend-of-doom-3ds.3dsx from the Homebrew Launcher.

Keep the included data folder with the executable; the standalone 3DSX download does not include those resources.

sdmc:/3ds/legend-of-doom/
├── legend-of-doom-3ds.3dsx
├── README.txt
├── CREDITS.md
├── THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md
├── licenses/
└── data/
    ├── LegendOfDoom.pk3
    ├── freedoom2.wad
    ├── game_support.pk3
    └── gzdoom.pk3

Audio setup

Audio on a real console requires its own DSP firmware at sdmc:/3ds/dspfirm.cdc. With Luma3DS, open the Rosalina menu, choose Miscellaneous options..., then Dump DSP firmware. This system file is not distributed with the port.

Features

A different view of Hyrule
The first-person Legend of Doom conversion, powered by GZDoom and Freedoom: Phase 2.		 Made for two screens
Touch menus, bottom-screen map and item selection, with Circle Pad and C-Stick controls.
Choose your setup
Install the CIA with its data, or use the complete Homebrew Launcher ZIP.		 Keep it current
Built-in CIA updates, save previews, native keyboard and quick diagnostic captures.

Feature details

  • Dual-screen menus, touch controls, a bottom-screen map and item selection.
  • Circle Pad movement and configurable C-Stick / touch camera input.
  • Save/load menus with previews and the native Nintendo 3DS keyboard.
  • Music and sound effects through OpenAL Soft/NDSP.
  • Adjustable gameplay render scale from 50% to 100%; menus use native 400×240.
  • A built-in CIA updater with stable and experimental channels.
  • Quick diagnostic capture for bug reports.

The published v1.0 uses the hardware-hybrid profile: SoftPoly renders the world on CPU0 and CPU2, and PICA200 scales the completed image to the 400×240 top screen. Gameplay defaults to 320×192. NovaGL world rendering remains a separate developer experiment. Rendering is uncapped; actual frame rate depends on the scene and render scale.

Controls

Nintendo 3DS input Action
Circle Pad Move / strafe
C-Stick Look
Touch screen Look when camera input is Touch or Both; select menu rows and items
A Use / interact; confirm in menus
B Back / cancel in menus
X Sprint at full health (optional)
Y Jump
L / R Alternate attack / attack
ZL / ZR Previous / next inventory item
D-Pad left / right Previous / next weapon
D-Pad down Use inventory item
D-Pad up Automap
START / SELECT Open the menu

Controller options include C-Stick sensitivity, C-Stick/Touch/Both camera input, the full-health X sprint toggle and a control reference.

Updating

On the CIA build, open Update from the title or pause menu. Choose Stable for public stable releases. Save your progress before installing an update, because installation closes the game. Saves and configuration remain on the SD card.

For 3DSX, download the complete matching ZIP and replace the executable and data together. The in-game updater installs CIA packages only. See the updater guide for channel behavior and troubleshooting.

Bug reports and community

Open a bug report with your version, console model, installation type and steps to reproduce the problem.

While the issue is visible, press L + R + A and attach the complete quick diagnostic folder from:

sdmc:/3ds/legend-of-doom/dumps/

For updater errors, also attach sdmc:/3ds/legend-of-doom/update.log.

Join Esteban's Forge on Discord for updates, support and other Nintendo 3DS homebrew projects.

Documentation

  • Repository map and maintenance conventions
Guide Purpose
3DS build guide Profiles, dependencies, package layout and checks.
Built-in updater CIA channels, installation and troubleshooting.
Maintenance roadmap Project documentation and development history.
Credits Original game conversion and platform contributors.

Building from source

Install devkitPro/devkitARM, libctru, 3ds-cmake, CMake, Python 3, Git, cURL and UnZip, plus a native C/C++ compiler and SDL2 development files for the host tools. CIA packaging also uses makerom and bannertool.

Build the same renderer profile used by the published v1.0:

./platform/3ds/build.sh hardware-hybrid

Calling the script without a profile builds the hardware-safe CPU-only recovery profile. GitHub Actions also builds that recovery profile; its artifacts are separate from the published v1.0 download. Output packages are written to build-3ds/dist/ by default.

See the 3DS build guide for all profiles, dependencies, package names and checks, and the maintenance roadmap for the documentation history.

The GZDoom-derived source is distributed under GNU GPL v3.0. See LICENSE for the complete terms. Third-party code and data retain their component-specific terms and notices in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md. The engine license does not relicense the game data.

Each release tag provides its corresponding source through GitHub's source archives.

Legend of Doom's upstream repository does not declare a general open-source license. Its data is downloaded during the build and is not committed here; the original credits and component notices are preserved in the packages.

The Legend of Zelda and related names and content are owned by Nintendo. Doom and related names are owned by id Software and their respective rights holders. This unofficial fan project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, id Software or Bethesda.

Community and bug reports

Join the project Discord for updates, testing, suggestions and support. Use GitHub issues for reproducible reports, including your version, console model and steps to reproduce the problem. Review diagnostic captures before sharing them.

Mario Kart 64 3DS

Pick your kart. Bring the race with you.
Mario Kart 64, adapted for Nintendo 3DS.

Download · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Contribute · Community

Native Nintendo 3DS port of Mario Kart 64, based on SpaghettiKart, with a dual-screen interface, touch menus and customizable controls and display options.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

A legally obtained USA Mario Kart 64 ROM is required. No ROM or extracted game data is included.

Features

Race your way
Single-player Grand Prix, Time Trial, VS and Battle, with CPU opponents, random cups and AUTO spectator mode.		 Made for two screens
Top-screen racing, five HUD layouts, course maps and bottom-screen touch menus.
Tune the presentation
Adjust render scale, draw distance, filters, UI textures and display profiles.		 Keep it current
Built-in Stable and Experimental updates that preserve your game data, saves and settings.

Download and installation

  1. Download the CIA or 3DSX from the releases page.
  2. Install the CIA with FBI, or use the 3DSX with the Homebrew Launcher.
  3. Place your USA ROM at sd:/3ds/MK64/mk64.z64.
  4. Launch the port. It validates the ROM and creates mk64.o2r on the SD card. Later launches reuse this archive.

The ROM must use .z64 byte order. Use the Hack64 ROM Swapper if conversion is needed. First-time extraction can take a while; keep the console charged.

For faster setup, download the MK64 Extractor for Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon or Linux x64 from the same release. Create mk64.o2r on your computer from your USA ROM, then copy it alongside your ROM:

sd:/3ds/MK64/mk64.z64
sd:/3ds/MK64/mk64.o2r

Use Options > Game > Update for built-in updates. See the updater guide for details.

Controls

Input Action
Circle Pad Steer
A Accelerate
B Brake / Reverse
R Hop / Drift
L Use item; open Options from Game Select
X Rear view
Y Cycle HUD layouts
C-Stick Hold for Turbo
Touch screen Navigate menus
SELECT Camera distance by default; configurable in Options
START Start / Pause / Continue

Mutiny 3DS

Pirates, cannons and a very angry seagull.
Nitrome's turn-based pirate artillery game, rebuilt natively for two Nintendo 3DS screens.

Download · Features · Documentation · Contribute · Credits

Native Nintendo 3DS port of Mutiny, the 2008 Flash game by Nitrome. The original ActionScript 2 game logic was rewritten in C, and the Flash animations play back through a small MovieClip runtime written for this port. The top screen shows the game. The bottom screen is a new touch interface drawn in pixel art.

This project was developed with the help of Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

Mutiny and all of its artwork, animation, music, sound, text and level design are © Nitrome. This is an unofficial fan port. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nitrome.

Features

Made for two screens
The game on top. Team health, a live minimap and the turn's controls on the touch screen below.		 The whole game
All 15 story levels, all 18 two-player battle maps and all 15 weapons, from cherry bombs to the tidal wave.
Throw with the stylus
Touch, pull back and let go. Slide across pirates and weapons to preview them, and drag the minimap to look around.		 Faithful to the original
Original animations, masks, sounds and music at the game's own 25 frames per second, drawn pixel-perfect.

Feature details

  • Story mode against the computer, with the original dialogue, scores, etc.
  • Two players on one console, taking turns on 18 battle maps. Treasure chests in two-player games hold 1 to 5 different random weapons, with 1 to 10 of each.
  • Bottom-screen interface: choose a pirate, pick a weapon, aim, place crates, barrels and anchors on the minimap, steer the parachute bomb, fire the cannon or send the tidal wave.
  • Test match: press START + SELECT together, in a menu or during a game, to start a two-player battle where every pirate carries 5 of every weapon.

Download and installation

Stable: v1.0. Requires a Nintendo 3DS family console with custom firmware (Luma3DS).

  1. Install the CIA with FBI. Scan the QR code from the release page with Remote Install → Scan QR Code, or copy the file to your SD card.
  2. Or copy the 3DSX to sdmc:/3ds/ and start it from the Homebrew Launcher.
  3. Start Mutiny from the HOME Menu. Progress and settings are saved to sdmc:/3ds/mutiny/mutiny.sav.

The application is self-contained: it needs no other files.

Audio

Audio requires a dumped DSP firmware. If you hear no sound, open the Luma3DS Rosalina menu and use:

Miscellaneous options > Dump DSP firmware

Controls

Input Action
Touch screen Everything: pirates, weapons, aiming, buttons and the minimap.
D-Pad / Circle Pad Move the camera, or the placement cursor.
A Confirm, or use the current action.
B Back.
L / R Previous / next pirate.
Y Slow placement cursor; switch the cannon between moving and aiming.
START Pause.
START + SELECT Start the all-weapons test match.

Documentation

Source map What every source file and tool does.
Development Extract the game data, build for macOS and 3DS, and run scripted tests.
Contributing How to report bugs and propose changes.
Changelog Changes in each release.
Build from source

You need your own copy of Mutiny.swf. The repository contains no Nitrome content: the build extracts and converts it locally. You also need devkitPro (devkitARM, libctru, citro2d, citro3d, bannertool, makerom), Java for JPEXS, Python 3 with Pillow and NumPy, FFmpeg, and CMake with SDL3 for the macOS build.

tools/extract.sh path/to/Mutiny.swf
tools/.venv/bin/python -I tools/gen_ui.py build/extract assets/ui
tools/.venv/bin/python -I tools/gen_lines.py build/extract src/game/lines.h
tools/.venv/bin/python -I tools/gen_3ds_meta.py
tools/build_3ds.sh          # build/3ds/mutiny.3dsx and mutiny.cia

See the development guide for the full setup.

pages.html:/repos/EstebanPdN/sm64ds-3ds/readme:
Super Mario 64 DS 3DS

Return to the castle. Take both screens with you.
A native Super Mario 64 DS port in development for Nintendo 3DS.

Source · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Contribute · Community

A native Nintendo 3DS adaptation of Super Mario 64 DS, based on Sébastien Breton’s native port and Tango’s decompilation, with analog movement, a touch interface and configurable camera and presentation.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex. Learn more about the development process here.

In active development; source available, with no public binary release yet. See Compatibility for BUILD 24 test coverage and remaining Old/New 3DS hardware qualification.

Features

Explore with analog controls
Circle Pad movement, touch controls and a free C-stick camera on compatible systems. Configurable movement modes.		 Made for two screens
Native upper-screen 3D, stereoscopic presentation and dedicated lower-screen pause and options menus.
Prepare once, load directly
A single .sm64ds companion, prepared locally from your compatible European ROM and read directly from SD.		 Keep settings and track problems
Persistent options, audio controls, backup recovery and a visible BUILD number for reproducible bug reports.

The original simulation and visual presentation use separate clocks. The optional 60 Hz presentation path interpolates eligible frames; it is not a claim of sustained 60 FPS on either console model. See compatibility and evidence.

Source and installation

The current source is available here; there are no releases or binary downloads yet. Build instructions and required private inputs are in the build guide.

A compatible user-supplied European ASMP revision 0 Nintendo DS ROM is required. No ROM, prepared gameplay archive, firmware, save or raw memory dump is included. For a locally built CIA or 3DSX:

  1. Install the CIA with FBI, or launch the 3DSX through Homebrew Launcher.
  2. Put your compatible .nds ROM in SD:/3ds/sm64ds/, or copy a matching .sm64ds companion made with SM64DS Packer.
  3. Launch the port and let preparation complete. Preserve existing saves and settings when replacing a test build.
  4. In the original interactive introduction, touch the star itself to continue. The BUILD label appears at the lower left of the title, pause menu and options.

See SD data and recovery before moving files or replacing an older build. The integrated game and the historical model viewer have different inputs and application IDs; use the integrated ROM-only target.

Controls

Input Current use
Circle Pad Analog movement; configurable sensitivity and run threshold.
A / B / X / Y, L / R Game actions according to the selected controller and movement mode.
C-stick Configurable camera on compatible New systems.
START Open the in-game pause menu.
Touch screen Original interactions, pause, controller and options menus.
3D slider Stereoscopic presentation where supported by the display path.

Developer capture shortcuts and their disk-space implications are described in diagnostics.

Documentation

Guide Purpose
Documentation index Current guides and historical investigations.
Compatibility Supported input, model profiles and validation limits.
SD data ROM, companion, saves, settings and recovery.
Building Source pins, SDK, private inputs and packaging.
Architecture Startup, ownership, adapters, workers and caches.
Testing ROM-free checks, ARM gates and emulator/hardware evidence.
Repository map File placement and maintenance conventions.
Source provenance Dependencies, immutable pins and notices.
Roadmap Remaining acceptance work.

Development

Requirements for portable checks: Git, Python 3.11+, CMake 3.20+ and a C++17 compiler. Clone with the public motion-library submodule:

Clone and run the portable checks 
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/EstebanPdN/sm64ds-3ds.git
cd sm64ds-3ds
python3 scripts/check-repository.py
cmake -S . -B build/host -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build/host --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build/host --output-on-failure

The complete game additionally requires devkitPro/devkitARM, libctru, Citro3D, the pinned Python packages and the local inputs listed in Building. A clean source checkout does not contain those game inputs. Contributing explains the checks and compatibility contracts to preserve.

Community and bug reports

Join Discord for discussion and testing. Use GitHub issues for reproducible bugs, including the visible BUILD number, console model and steps to reproduce. Review logs and captures before sharing them; full process dumps and game data must remain private.

  • Nintendo — Super Mario 64 DS and original game content.
  • EstebanPdN — adaptation, interface, diagnostics and maintenance, with help from Codex.

See the full credits and third-party notices.

Starwing 3DS

Set course for Lylat. Take the squadron with you.
Star Fox / Starwing, adapted for Nintendo 3DS.

Download · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Contribute · Community

A Nintendo 3DS adaptation of the SNES Star Fox / Starwing, based on KandoWontU's Starfox Enhanced, UltraStarFox, and Team SFEX's work.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

This is an early release. The port is expected to be completable, but extensive playtesting is still pending. See Compatibility for the current scope.

Features

Take flight
Play the Original experience, with wide presentation and optional top HUD. Star Fox EX and stereoscopic depth are experimental.		 Made for two screens
Native 400×240 upper presentation, a separate 320×240 touch interface, Circle Pad and D-pad controls.
Pick up and play
Native SPC audio, volume settings, persistent options, per-ROM EX SRAM and optional checkpoints.		 Keep it current
Built-in Stable and Experimental updates, release notes, verified downloads and local diagnostics.

Original game speed, interpolation ON and a 60 FPS presentation limit are the defaults. Existing saved preferences are preserved. The limit is not a claim of sustained hardware FPS. Star Fox EX is not fully supported.

Download and installation

Supported systems: New Nintendo 3DS / New 2DS XL and Old Nintendo 3DS / 2DS. Old 3DS / 2DS support is new in 1.2 and experimental: busy scenes can show fewer frames than on New models. See Compatibility.

Release notes and FBI QR · Project website

  1. Install Starwing-3DS.cia with FBI, or scan the release's QR in Remote Install → Scan QR Code.
  2. Place your compatible, clean .sfc or .smc ROM in /3ds/Starwing/ on SD.
  3. Launch Starwing. The game validates your ROM and builds its companion locally.
  4. Use Options → Game Version for Original / EX and ROM Files to select another ROM. Keep your existing SD data when upgrading.

The 3DSX is also available for Homebrew Launcher. A compatible user-supplied ROM is required; no ROM download is provided. Supported revisions, upgrade behavior, settings, and files are covered in SD data.

The built-in Options → Update checks this repository for future releases. See Updating for installation and recovery.

Controls

Input Action
Circle Pad / D-pad SNES movement; D-pad takes priority.
A / B / X / Y, L / R Corresponding SNES buttons; the chosen in-game control scheme assigns their actions.
START / SELECT SNES controls, subject to enabled diagnostic shortcuts.
Touch screen Options, game selection, and diagnostic cards.

Development

Requirements for the ROM-free checks: Python 3, Bash, a C++20 compiler, pkg-config, and Jansson development headers.

git clone https://github.com/EstebanPdN/starwing-3ds.git
cd starwing-3ds
python3 tools/check-publication.py
bash tools/test-host.sh

A full game build additionally needs devkitPro and the locally prepared inputs in the build guide. The clean source checkout alone does not generate a playable package. See Contributing before changing timing, rendering, data formats, or the platform boundary.

Join the project Discord for updates, testing, suggestions, and support. Use GitHub issues for reproducible reports. Capture shortcuts and sharing precautions are in Diagnostics.

A Link to the Past 3DS

Return to Hyrule. Keep the map close.
A Link to the Past, adapted for two Nintendo 3DS screens.

Download · Features · Documentation · Changelog · Community

Nintendo 3DS dual-screen port of Zelda3.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

This project is based on open-source work from:

  • Original reverse-engineered Zelda3 engine: https://github.com/snesrev/zelda3
  • Android port base: https://github.com/Waterdish/zelda3-android
  • Dual-screen Android branch used as the 3DS source base: https://github.com/samyost1/zelda3-android

No ROM or extracted game asset package is distributed in this repository. Each user must provide their own legally obtained USA, unheadered ROM on their own 3DS SD card.

Version 4.1 adds Japanese game and menus, direct .zspr skins, language corrections and fixes for WIDE, maps, menus and new randomizer seeds. The port supports eight languages, character mods, a native randomizer and fifteen quality-of-life options. See development and build boundaries for source organization and the disabled developer scenarios.

Features

Return to Hyrule
A native dual-screen adaptation based on Zelda3 and its Android ports.		 Made for two screens
400×240 gameplay above; live maps, gear, items and touch settings below.
Choose your view
Wide, stretched and original presentation, with persistent per-ROM settings and turbo options.		 Keep it current
Stable / Pre-release updates, on-device ROM extraction and quick diagnostic checkpoints.

Feature details

  • Top screen: 400x240 gameplay.
  • Bottom screen: 320x240 live map, dungeon map, gear view, item selection and touch settings.
  • First launch extracts zelda3_assets.dat locally from the user's ROM.
  • Display modes: wide mod, stretched original and original aspect.
  • Turbo speed: off, x2, x3, x4 or x5.
  • New 3DS: ZL or C-stick can hold turbo when turbo is enabled.
  • Quick diagnostics: press L + R + A to create a dump with memory files, physical 400x240/320x240 screen captures, raw display framebuffers and a validated load-state.bin checkpoint. Audio pauses during capture and a DUMP SAVED notice confirms complete success on the top screen.
  • Developer settings can load the newest dump checkpoint for the active ROM profile and optionally show the current FPS on the top screen.
  • PICA200/Citro2D presentation for both screens with nearest-neighbor sampling and RGB565 display output.
  • PICA200 GPU rendering on Old 3DS, with automatic software fallback for unsupported effects. New 3DS uses its existing CPU renderer.
  • Native 400x240 WIDE mode, fixed-camera edge corrections and persistent per-ROM display, zoom, turbo and control settings.
  • Responsive map controls and independent heart updates on Old 3DS.
  • Fixed-step 60 Hz gameplay timing with bounded catch-up instead of making game speed depend on when a VBlank wait returns.
  • Parallel PPU scanline rendering on Core 0 and Core 1, plus Core 2 on New 3DS, with persistent tile-row caches and frame-time diagnostics in quick dumps.
  • HOME Menu banner uses a lightweight custom CGFX 3D logo model with the supplied hover sound converted to a short PCM WAV.

Download and installation

Stable: v4.1.

Install the CIA, then create this directory on the SD card:

sdmc:/3ds/Zelda 3DS/

Place a legally obtained USA, unheadered ROM there. The preferred filename is zelda3.sfc, but the setup also accepts other .sfc or .smc filenames.

On first launch, press A to validate the ROM and extract the assets. The ROM is read locally and is never copied into the CIA.

If you’re using a translated/patched ROM, put both the clean USA ROM and the patched ROM in sdmc:/3ds/Zelda 3DS/.

The port should use the clean ROM for the original assets and the patched ROM for the translated text. Translation patches may work this way, but gameplay hacks are not guaranteed to be compatible.

Audio requires:

sdmc:/3ds/dspfirm.cdc

Luma3DS can create this file from the console's own firmware through Rosalina's Dump DSP firmware command.

Releases

Every GitHub release includes:

  • installable CIA
  • Homebrew Launcher 3DSX
  • QR code for scanning the CIA URL from FBI on a 3DS

GitHub supplies automatic source-code archives for each tag. The release page shows the QR code, a short changelog and bug-report instructions. Detailed development notes are preserved inside the source snapshot.

Latest stable release: v4.1

See CHANGELOG.md for the changes since v2.8.

Updates

In Settings > Update, choose Stable or Pre-release. Tap the release name to read its changelog on the top screen, with Prev/Next below for more pages. Choose Download Update and confirm installation, then reopen the game. Save in-game before installing. Startup checks also indicate newer releases.

Version v4.1 is the latest stable release. Select the Stable channel to install it.

Settings is Screen, Turbo Speed, Developer, Update, Restart. Restart returns to the startup home and starts the game fresh; existing saves remain.

Version 3.1 uses the native HID contact flag for touch press and release detection, including startup and releases with residual coordinates. Physical coordinates remain protected from SDL viewport transforms. The last 32 touch selections are included in diagnostic dumps. Use the FBI QR if touch controls prevent opening Update.

pages.html:/repos/EstebanPdN/zelda-tmc-3ds/rea:
The Minish Cap 3DS

A small hero. A two-screen adventure.
The Minish Cap, adapted for Nintendo 3DS.

Download · Features · Documentation · Contribute · Community

Nintendo 3DS dual-screen port of The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap, based on the open-source Minish Cap decompilation, Project Picori, and the dual-screen Android port.

This project was developed with the help of OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Learn more about the development process here.

This project is based on open-source work from:

  • samyost1/tmc-android — dual-screen Android source base
  • Project Picori — native Minish Cap engine and port infrastructure
  • zeldaret/tmc — original decompilation

No ROM or extracted Nintendo game assets are distributed with this project. You must provide your own legally obtained compatible Game Boy Advance ROM.

Features

Explore a smaller world
Native Minish Cap gameplay with USA and European ROM support and regional backports.		 Made for two screens
Wide top-screen gameplay with maps, quest status, touch items and settings below.
Choose your presentation
Wide, Original and Stretch modes; Blur, Bilinear and Pixel Perfect styles.		 Keep it current
Stable / Pre-release updates, persistent settings, native audio and diagnostic checkpoints.

Feature details

  • Native Nintendo 3DS port with full dual-screen support.
  • Supports both USA and European ROMs with automatic region detection.
  • Includes native European gameplay backports; no patched ROM is required.
  • True widescreen gameplay on the 400x240 top screen, plus Original and Stretch display modes.
  • Bottom-screen interface with live map, dungeon information, quest status, touch item controls, and settings. The opening Picori legend keeps the bottom screen black; the overworld map shows only its stone frame until Link receives it.
  • New 3DS enhancements including 804 MHz mode, L2 cache, multi-core rendering, and optional 2x–5x turbo using the C-Stick.
  • Three display styles: Blur, Bilinear, and Pixel Perfect.
  • Aspect and filter selections are independent; Wide + Pixel Perfect uses the normal widescreen camera.
  • In-app updates with Stable and Pre-release channels, top-screen changelogs, and verified CIA/3DSX installation.
  • Native stereo audio, persistent settings, reliable save handling, FPS tools, and diagnostic dumps for bug reports.

Performance

The port automatically selects a performance profile for the detected console.

New Nintendo 3DS keeps the full-presentation path with 804 MHz mode, L2 cache, multi-core rendering, and C-Stick turbo.

Old Nintendo 3DS uses an optimized renderer, lower-overhead audio path, and adaptive presentation-skip profile. When rendering cannot sustain 60 visual FPS, the engine can continue advancing near its 60 Hz target instead of slowing the entire game down. Input, touch, audio, and lifecycle handling continue to run on skipped presentation ticks.

The bottom-screen worker avoids redundant static redraws while keeping touch input sampled on every engine tick.

Download and installation

Stable: v2.2.

v2.2 includes the normal-save compatibility fix from v2.2-E1 and removes the experimental filter-dependent camera mode. Install it over the existing application and keep your .sav and companion files. Known inactive legacy metadata is accepted without deletion; active or unrecognized profiles remain protected.

  1. Install the CIA with FBI, or use the 3DSX build with the Homebrew Launcher.
tmc-3ds-v2.2.cia
  1. Create this folder on your SD card:
sdmc:/3ds/The Minish Cap 3DS/
  1. Place your legally obtained USA or European .gba ROM inside that folder.

The ROM can have any filename as long as it uses the .gba extension.

Recommended ROM

Both the USA and European versions are supported, but I highly recommend using the European ROM.

The European version is the ROM I used throughout the development and testing of this port, so it has received by far the most testing.

The USA version should be compatible, but it behaves slightly differently in some parts of the game, so you may encounter bugs that are not present when using the European version.

The European ROM also includes multiple languages, including English, so there is generally no disadvantage to using it.

Expected clean ROM SHA-1 values:

USA:    b4bd50e4131b027c334547b4524e2dbbd4227130
Europe: cff199b36ff173fb6faf152653d1bccf87c26fb7

The ROM stays on your SD card and is never included in the CIA.

Audio

Audio requires a working Nintendo 3DS DSP firmware setup.

If homebrew audio is not working, open the Luma3DS Rosalina Menu and use:

Miscellaneous options > Dump DSP firmware

Diagnostics

If you encounter a crash, graphical bug, performance problem, or anything unusual, press:

L + R + A

The port will pause and create a diagnostic dump containing screenshots, memory information, runtime state, performance data, and other information that can help identify the problem.

Dumps are saved under:

sdmc:/3ds/The Minish Cap 3DS/dumps/

Gameplay dumps also include a validated load-state.bin checkpoint. To reproduce the most recent dump, open:

Settings > Developer > Load State

New sessions use 000-dump-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS, 001-dump-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS, and so on. The sequence survives restarts and clock changes; an emptied dumps folder starts again at 000.

The loader asks for confirmation, selects the newest numbered folder (or a legacy dump-* folder), and rejects corrupted checkpoints or checkpoints created with a different ROM region. Older dumps that only contain save-state.bin remain supported, but they resume from the saved checkpoint rather than the exact captured position.

Please send the dump when reporting bugs whenever possible.

Updates

Open Settings > Update. Select Stable or Pre-release, then tap the release version to read its changelog on the top screen. Use Prev / Next to turn pages. Download Update asks for confirmation before downloading and installing. Save your game first: the application closes after a successful update.

CIA builds overwrite only this application's title after checking its ID and SHA-256 digest. 3DSX builds replace the launched file with rollback protection. Wi-Fi is required; connection failures leave the current installation available.

Nimbus

Pretendo account manager for the 3DS

Usage

  1. Grab the latest app and IPS patches from the Releases page
  2. Extract to the root of your 3DS SD card
  3. Install the Nimbus homebrew using FBI (or FBI Reloaded) if using the CIA build
  4. Run the Nimbus homebrew and select either to use a Pretendo or Nintendo account
    • If it doesn't work, reboot your 3DS while holding SELECT and ensure that "Enable loading external FIRMs and modules" and "Enable game patching" are both turned on, as well as ensuring that your Luma3DS version is 13.0 or higher.
  5. Enable the Nimbus plugin by entering into the Rosalina menu and setting the "Plugin Loader" to "Enabled"

Building

  1. Clone the repository recursively using git clone https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus --recursive
    • If you have cloned the repository previously, please run git pull and make clean while in the nimbus folder to avoid errors and broken files
    • On top of that, if you cloned it before 1.0.2 released, you might also need to run git submodule update --init --recursive while in the nimbus folder
  2. Install devkitARM, libctru 2.5.0 or later, 3ds-curl, 3ds-mbedtls, 3ds-zlib, CTRPluginFramework, 3gxtool, armips, makerom, bannertool and flips
  3. Copy decompressed code.bin files from the act, friends, http, miiverse, socket and ssl sysmodules in their respective patches directories (any Miiverse code.bin works for the miiverse module)
  4. Run make

Credits

Thanks to:

  • pinklimes for the CIA version banner
  • TraceEntertains for making a CIA version of Nimbus and maintaining the project
  • DaniElectra for making the 3DS HTTP and Socket patches and maintaining the project
  • SciresM for making the 3DS SSL patches
  • zaksabeast for the original 3ds-Friend-Account-Manager and all the research into the friends and act system titles
  • shutterbug2000 for the GUI
  • libctru for the frda.c base, homebrew template, and other library functions (and thanks to citro2d for part of a system font function)
  • Universal-Core for the string drawing functions
  • Fangal-Airbag for making the account switcher GUI support button controls
  • All other 3DS researchers

json:/repos/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/relea.body:
## Important Note

Unlike Nimbus v2.0.0-rc1, this release doesn't require any special steps when upgrading from either v1.6.1 or older nor from this release candidate. When updating to this version, the patches will not be applied until you open the application, in which case it will deploy the update files on their proper location and handle any migration procedures automatically.

## What's New

- **Improvements on account management and error handling.** If an error happens while switching accounts, they will be reported on screen for easier debugging.
- **New multi-purpose plugin.** This plugin bundles patches for game exploits, a PID logger for a bunch of games and HokakuCTR. This plugin must be activated each time you want to use it from the Nimbus app by pressing the Y button.

### FAQ: When switching accounts I sometimes get the following error: d8a0c4e5

**Short explanation:** This error is very uncommon, but it can be fixed by trying again or disabling Wi-Fi to ensure it doesn't happen.

**Long explanation:**

Before switching accounts, the system must be logged out from any accounts to be able to switch to another one. However, the friends sysmodule requires to be disconnected from the friends server in order to log out, or it will throw `FPD::Connected`, the error from above. There isn't any API available to "disconnect" from the server, so the way it works is by blocking the network connection (in a similar way as when switching from Internet to Local Play) to get the friends sysmodule to disconnect from the server.

Our code checks for when the friends sysmodule actually gets disconnected, so this error shouldn't in theory happen, but there have been very rare instances of this error popping up despite the fact. As mentioned, this issue can be fixed by retrying the account switch or disabling Wi-Fi on the console full stop to ensure it always disconnects successfully.

## What's Changed
* [Important] Fix Miiverse patch misattribution and missing license by @TraceEntertains in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/51
* feat: Improve account management by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/54
* feat: Add PNID migration tool and bump version to 2.0.0 by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/63
* feat: Add Nimbus plugin by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/65
* chore: Point support to our Discord server by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/67
* feat: Make the Nimbus app deploy the update by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/68


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/compare/v1.6.1...v2.0.0

## BREAKING CHANGES :warning:

This new release requires user intervention for existing installations. Please check below for how to install this update. **You MUST follow this procedure EXACTLY, or your PNID will be removed and you'll have to take some recovery steps**.
 - If you are installing Nimbus for the first time, you can skip this section.
 - If you have connected to Pretendo in the past but don't have a PNID linked to your console, you MUST still follow these steps, or you will have problems when linking one in the future.

### Update steps

1. Install the `nimbus.3dsx` or `nimbus.cia` file **ONLY. DO NOT COPY ANY OTHER FILES YET!**
2. Launch the new version of Nimbus
  2.1. The new version of Nimbus should show the version `2.0.0` on the bottom-right corner of the top screen. If this isn't the case, verify that you are launching the correct version and you have installed everything properly.
3. Press the B button to save your PNID
4. If everything goes well, Nimbus will show a success message
  4.1. If Nimbus shows an error, ask on our [Discord](https://discord.gg/pretendo) or the [forum](https://forum.pretendo.network/) for assistance
5. Press START to exit Nimbus and copy all of the other files for the update. You should now be good to go!

### Recovery steps

If you have copied all of the Nimbus files and you haven't saved your PNID, you have to follow these recovery steps:

1. **Ensure you have installed Nimbus 2.0.0 correctly and that the version shows on screen when opening it**
2. If you are connected to Pretendo, open Nimbus and switch to the Nintendo account. If you are already connected to Nintendo, skip to the next step
  2.1. This is required because the Pretendo account is now in a bugged state where it has a Pretendo Friend Code but it's linked to your **Nintendo NNID**, because the **Pretendo PNID** was deleted from the system
3. Open Nimbus and switch to the Pretendo account
  3.1. This will recreate the Pretendo PNID and link the Pretendo account back to it
4. After this, opening the NNID settings should now show the account creation and linking screen properly

## What's New

- **Improvements on account management and error handling.** If an error happens while switching accounts, they will be reported on screen for easier debugging.
- **New multi-purpose plugin.** This plugin bundles patches for game exploits, a PID logger for a bunch of games and HokakuCTR. This plugin must be activated each time you want to use it from the Nimbus app by pressing the Y button.

### FAQ: When switching accounts I sometimes get the following error: d8a0c4e5

**Short explanation:** This error is very uncommon, but it can be fixed by trying again or disabling Wi-Fi to ensure it doesn't happen.

**Long explanation:**

Before switching accounts, the system must be logged out from any accounts to be able to switch to another one. However, the friends sysmodule requires to be disconnected from the friends server in order to log out, or it will throw `FPD::Connected`, the error from above. There isn't any API available to "disconnect" from the server, so the way it works is by blocking the network connection (in a similar way as when switching from Internet to Local Play) to get the friends sysmodule to disconnect from the server.

Our code checks for when the friends sysmodule actually gets disconnected, so this error shouldn't in theory happen, but there have been very rare instances of this error popping up despite the fact. As mentioned, this issue can be fixed by retrying the account switch or disabling Wi-Fi on the console full stop to ensure it always disconnects successfully.

## What's Changed
* [Important] Fix Miiverse patch misattribution and missing license by @TraceEntertains in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/51
* feat: Improve account management by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/54
* feat: Add PNID migration tool and bump version to 2.0.0 by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/63
* feat: Add Nimbus plugin by @DaniElectra in https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/pull/65


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nimbus/compare/v1.6.1...v2.0.0-rc1

pages.html:/repos/SecondaryLifer/StarHaven/rea:
Star Haven

A native Nintendo 3DS port of Paper Mario (Nintendo 64), built from the Paper Mario decompilation. The game's own C code runs on the 3DS; nothing is emulated.


▶ Watch Star Haven running on a 3DS

Star Haven contains no game data. You need your own Paper Mario ROM (EU, US, or the iQue Player's Chinese release).

Join the Star Haven 3DS Discord: discord.gg/zHq9tH49Z for help, news about new versions and to report bugs. Bug reports here on GitHub are welcome too.

Install

  1. On a 3DS with custom firmware, open FBI → Remote Install → Scan QR Code and scan the code on the right. It always installs the newest release. You can also download StarHaven.cia or StarHaven.3dsx from Releases.
  2. Copy your ROM into /3ds/StarHaven/ on the SD card. Any file name works, and so do .z64, .n64 and .v64 dumps.
  3. Start Star Haven from the HOME menu.

Full instructions: the player readme.

Bring your N64 or Paperboat save

Got a Paper Mario save from Project64, RetroArch, ares, a flashcart or the Wii U Virtual Console? Keep playing it on the 3DS:

  • In the game: put the save in /3ds/StarHaven/ as import.fla (a RetroArch .srm as import.srm) and start Star Haven. It converts the save and keeps your old one as save.fla.bak.
  • In a browser: the save converter turns an N64 save into a Star Haven save.fla / save_us.fla, and a Star Haven save back into an N64 one. Nothing is uploaded.
  • From Paperboat (PC): drop its file0.json to file3.json into the same converter to get a save_us.fla, or a save_us.fla to get Paperboat files back (US ROM only, like Paperboat).

Features

  • EU and US versions in one package
  • 60 fps (in-between frames are added), or the original 30
  • Fast-forward and faster text
  • Original, Fill or Wide screen, the 3D slider with a depth setting, remappable buttons
  • A touch bottom screen with its tabs down the side:
    • Stats, with a quick-save button and what the area and the room you are in still hide
    • Map: the world map, showing where you are
    • Party: tap a partner to switch to them
    • Tattle: every enemy Goombario has tattled so far; tap one to read the whole tattle
    • Found: star pieces, badges, hidden blocks and panels and item spots collected in each area
    • Recipes: every dish Tayce T. cooks, the ones you've made, and how to make each one
    • plus Items, and in battle your HP, FP and Star Power down the side and the menus to tap: Mario's commands as big tiles with the game's icons, and targets picked on a live picture of the stage
  • A randomizer, chosen when you start a new file, with a seed you can share
  • Optional cheats (infinite HP, FP and Star Power, 999 coins, unlimited BP) for files started with them on (chosen once, when the file is made)
  • Imports N64 saves (Project64, RetroArch, Wii U Virtual Console and others), and a web converter for both directions, also to and from Paperboat
  • 60 fps on the New 3DS family; about 30 fps on the original 3DS and 2DS, with a few extras off there (CIA only)
  • Tells you on the bottom screen when a newer version is out (one check at start, nothing is downloaded; Options can turn it off)
World map Party: tap a partner to switch Options
Tattle log Tap an enemy to read its tattle Found: what you collected in each area
New file: Classic or Randomizer What the randomizer shuffles

Building

See port/3ds/README.md. Everything builds in a Docker image with devkitARM, libctru and citro3d, and needs your own ROMs in ver/pal/ and ver/us/.

Layout
port/3ds/ the 3DS port: platform layer, renderer, audio, tools, packaging
src/, include/, ver/ the decompilation, with port changes under #ifdef _3DS
DECOMP_README.md the decompilation's own readme

Credits

  • 3D HOME Menu banner by Velvii. The title is in the Hey Gorgeous font, free for personal use.

License

The port (everything under port/3ds/ and the port's changes to the decompilation) is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, copyright 2026 SecondaryLifer. Forks are welcome; keep the NOTICE file and credit Star Haven by SecondaryLifer. The decompilation itself is pmret/papermario.

Legal

Star Haven is a fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. Paper Mario is a trademark of Nintendo. Release packages contain no Nintendo game data: images, models, sounds and text are read from the player's own ROM at startup. The screenshots show the game running on the port.

• Updating works again: every Star Haven CIA so far carried the wrong version number inside (1.3.3 showed as 1.0.3), so FBI thought 1.3.x was older than 1.2.x and refused to install it. 1.3.4 has the right one and installs over any older version. Thanks to lithyc for spotting it (#73)!

  • Lava Piranha softlock fixed: fighting the Lava Piranha a second time in one session (after a game over, for example) could get stuck after its fake defeat. Fast-forward also pauses itself in its room now (#66).

  • Randomizer: a new Badge costs option: badges swap their BP and FP costs, listed in the spoiler file. Speedy Spin keeps its cost.

If you're on 1.3.0–1.3.3 and FBI says a newer version is installed: delete Star Haven in FBI (Titles) first, then install. Your saves stay on the SD card.

You need your own Paper Mario ROM (EU or US). Put it on the SD card in /3ds/StarHaven/ (any file name; .z64, .n64 and .v64 all work). Star Haven contains no game data.

  • StarHaven.cia: install with FBI, or scan this with FBI → Remote Install → Scan QR Code:

  • StarHaven.3dsx: for the Homebrew Launcher (New 3DS family)

Coming from 1.0.0 or 1.0.1? 1.0.2 changed the title ID, so delete the old Star Haven icon after installing (FBI → Titles, or System Settings → Data Management). Saves are kept.

pages.html:/repos/Steveice10/FBI/readme:
FBI

FBI is an open source title manager for the 3DS.

Download: https://github.com/Steveice10/FBI/releases

Requires devkitARM, along with 3ds-curl, 3ds-zlib, and 3ds-jansson from the devkitPro pacman repository, to build.

Features

  • Browse and modify the SD card, TWL photos, TWL sounds, save data, and ext save data.

  • Export, import, and erase save data from DS cartridges.

  • Export, import, and delete save data secure values.

  • Install titles/tickets from a file system, over a local network, or over the Internet with a URL or QR code.

    • Automatically imports title seeds on installation, either from the Internet or the SD card.

  • Browse and delete pending titles (downloaded updates, in-progress eShop titles, etc).

  • Customize appearance by placing replacements for RomFS resources in "sdmc:/fbi/theme/".

  • Only available when run from a CIA, 3DS, or a 3DSX under Luma3DS:

    • Browse and modify CTR NAND, TWL NAND, and system save data.
    • Dump the raw NAND image to the SD card.
    • Launch titles installed to the system.

Credit

Banner: Originally created by OctopusRift, touched up by Apache Thunder, updated for new logo by PabloMK7.

Logo: PabloMK7

SPI Protocol Information: TuxSH (TWLSaveTool)

pages.html:/repos/Universal-Team/Universal-Upd:
An easy to use app for installing and updating 3DS homebrew

Universal-Updater is a homebrew application for the Nintendo 3DS with the intention to make downloading other homebrew simple and easy. No need to manually copy files or go through installation processes, as it does that all for you.

Features

  • A store format with a concept similar to the Cydia Repositories
    • The default is Universal-DB
    • Want to add more? Go to settings, choose "Select Unistore", click the + icon and select one from the list, enter a URL, or scan a QR code
  • Customization in sorting and display
    • Several sorting keys: "Title", "Author", and "Last Updated"
    • Direction can be Ascending or Descending
    • App display can be shown in either a grid or rows
  • Background installation so you can keep using the rest of the app while installing
  • Searching and markings to make finding apps easy
  • Viewing screenshots and release notes for apps
  • Shortcuts for easily updating frequently updated apps when using the Homebrew Launcher
  • Translations for users of many languages
    • To contribute to translations, join our Crowdin project
    • To request a new language, join our Discord Server or contact a project manager on Crowdin

Compilation

Setting up your environment

To build Universal-Updater from source, you will need to install devkitARM and some libraries. Follow devkitPro's Getting Started page to install pacman, then run the following command to install everything you need:

(sudo dkp-)pacman -S 3ds-dev 3ds-curl 3ds-bzip2 3ds-libarchive 3ds-liblzma 3ds-libzstd

(The sudo dkp- may not be needed depending on your OS)

You will also need bannertool and makerom in your PATH.

Cloning the repository

To download the source you will need to clone the repository with submodules, this can be done by running:

git clone --recursive https://github.com/Universal-Team/Universal-Updater.git

If you've already cloned it, you can use the following command to update all of the submodules:

git submodule update --init --recursive

Building

Once you've cloned the repository (with submodules), simply run make in the root of the repository.

This release fixes an odd bug from v3.4.0 where the metadata file (containing marks and the update status of apps) stopped saving, thanks @syndenbock for the report! I also fixed a bug I'd noticed where Universal-Updater could crash if you exited while a thread was running. Italian and Russian translations have also been updated, thanks to everyone who's helped with translations!

See [v3.4.0's Release notes][v340] for full details on recent changes, the highlights were:

- Universal-Updater now tracks installed apps (displayed by an SD card icon) and this can be used for filtering!
- Added a "NOT" filtering option to invert the filter, most useful for filtering to only apps not installed
- The search menu now includes all app names in the word completion dictionary!
- Proxies are now properly supported!
- The SSL CA certificate bundle is now be loaded from the SD card instead of RomFS

json:/repos/Universal-Team/Universal-Upd.name: Install checking, proxies, and more
json:/repos/Universal-Team/Universal-Upd.body:
Proxy users rejoice! One of the oldest issues on the tracker that no one had had the motivation to test properly, proxies should now be fully supported. Universal-Updater also now checks for what you have installed on your system and shows it with a little icon by the app icon. This lets you filter to easily find apps you already have installed or if you've got a lot on your system you can now flip the filters and instead show only new apps!

### Features
- Universal-Updater now tracks installed apps (displayed by an SD card icon) and this can be used for filtering! (Thanks @TrianguloY for the icon!)
   - NOTE: The tracking is done by title ID and file path so conflicting apps will be displayed even if not installed (ex. HBL forks)
- Added a "NOT" filtering option to invert the filter, most useful for filtering to only apps not installed
- The search menu now includes all app names in the word completion dictionary!
- Proxies are now properly supported! (Thanks @lxfly2000)
   - By default the system proxy will be used as HTTP, but other types of proxies supported by curl can be set in settings

### Changes
- The SSL CA certificate bundle will now be loaded from the SD card instead of ROMFS
   - Uses the location from Luma3DS (`sdmc:/config/ssl/cacert.pem`)
   - Other homebrew desiring SSL peer verification are encouraged to use that location too, Universal-Updater will ensure it exists and is valid on load
      - NOTE: Updating the CA certificate bundle on console in this way is technically a security hole as you're downloading your source of trust from an unverified host... that said, its 3DS homebrew, its not that big a deal; but get the file manually from Luma3DS or curl if worried
   - Users are now presented with the option to disable peer verification if they really don't want to fix their system date or update their certificate bundle
- Universal-Updater now waits for a Wi-Fi connection on startup, previously it was possible to have the initial UniStore download fail if your 3DS was still trying to establish the connection
- The "select UniStore" menu now loads the UniStore list in a separate thread making for a more responsive menu
- A spinner is now shown when Universal-Updater is doing something in the background but user input is possible
   - This is intended to draw attention to the fact that something can happen if you wait (or perform an outside action like syncing the time) and that skipping is not your only option
- Updated for latest libctru

### Bug fixes
- Fixed the list view cutting off one item when under 4 exist
- Universal-Updater now has the correct app title on the HOME Menu
- The update check (used for most internet sanity checks too) now pulls from Universal-DB instead of the GitHub API, hopefully reducing confusing errors

A much smaller release than the last one, but with some nice changes nonetheless.

New features

  • Much improved search menu
    • I had always intended to make the search menu have buttons or dropdowns or the like for the Categories and Consoles values, well it took a hot minute but now it's here!
    • You can also search on descriptions now, by default searches now search both title or description, but you can disable either of them
  • (@Epicpkmn11 and @Sorunome) SSL validity is now actually checked and respected
    • Previously while we fully supported SSL for encryption, we had certificate validation disabled leaving MITM attacks possible
    • Minor downside is that web requests will now properly fail if your date is set significantly off, but this is easy to fix from Luma3DS's Rosalina menu
  • Several menus that previously required using the buttons to scroll are now fully controllable on the touch screen by scrolling on tapping the first or last item in the list
  • Prompt messages now automatically wrap text and support scrolling!
  • Added a warning on start if the connection times out that you probably have an incompatible custom DNS
  • Replaced our old practice of uploading commit builds to a dedicated repository with uploading them to a 'git' release on this repo
    • This makes them easier to find and fixes some buggy behaviour when using the git build auto-update feature in app
    • We have also changed the nomenclature from 'nightly builds' to 'git builds' as it better reflects the technical reality

Bug fixes

  • Fixed sleep mode!
    • Universal-Updater used to block sleep mode despite it not actually keeping an internet connection so battery was wasted for no reason; now sleep is only blocked while the queue is running and downloads actually work! (your console will finish all downloads and installs then go to sleep)
  • Fixed visual regression in v3.3.0 that made the install confirmation unhelpfully always ask if you're sure you want to install the first entry rather than the selected one
  • Made it so the install confirmation prompt is never skipped for nightlies and pre-releases
